chapters.title: Chapter 1751: Witch God Valley!
paragraphs: Max did not even look back.
"We do not have time for them."

The moment he said those words, golden light erupted from his body and expanded outward, forming a wide shield around both him and Nancy. The shield was not a simple barrier. It was formed from the power of his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, and its surface glowed with sacred golden patterns that moved like flowing sunlight.

The moment the black-winged insects crashed into it, their bodies were burned into ashes by the radiance before their mouths could even touch the surface. The thorn-covered vines whipped against the shield again and again, but every strike only caused ripples of light to spread across it, while the poisonous liquid they released evaporated the instant it touched the golden barrier.
The three-headed demonic bird came next.

It opened its mouths and released three beams of dark, rotten energy, each one filled with a cursed force that could corrode flesh and soul, but Max only raised one hand slightly while continuing to fly upward.

The golden shield brightened, and the three beams struck its surface with a thunderous explosion, causing the clouds around them to scatter and the nearby branches to tremble, yet the shield did not break. Not even a crack appeared.
The attack was swallowed by the golden light, and Max flew straight through the storm of rotten wind as if nothing had happened.
Nancy looked at the shield around them and felt her heart calm slightly.

She had been worried that they would be delayed by the creatures living on the Witch God Tree, but Max clearly had no intention of fighting them one by one. He simply used absolute defense and terrifying speed to ignore everything in their path.

No matter what attacked them, whether it was cursed insects, demonic birds, soul-devouring flowers, living roots, shadow beasts hidden in the bark, or strange black spirits that crawled out from the mist, all of them were blocked by the golden shield before they could reach either of them.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Attack after attack landed against the shield.
Claws struck it.
Fangs bit into it.
Curses spread across it.
Illusion mist tried to seep through it.
Dark lightning fell from the clouds above and crashed down upon it.
Yet none of these attacks could stop Max.

The golden shield remained steady around him and Nancy, and Max continued flying upward with his eyes fixed on the unseen top of the tree. His expression was calm, but his speed only grew faster with every passing moment, as if the dangers around him were nothing more than wind brushing against his face.

Nancy followed closely within the protection of the shield, and although she kept her guard up, she soon realized that unless something truly terrifying appeared, there was no need for her to make a move at all.
The higher they went, the stranger the Witch God Tree became.

The bark around them was no longer only dark brown and gray-black. It began to show faint purple veins that pulsed like blood vessels beneath the surface. Some branches were covered in glowing white flowers shaped like tiny skulls, while other branches were completely dead, twisted, and covered in chains of black moss that moved as if alive.

Huge hollows opened in the trunk from time to time, and within those hollows, Max could sense sleeping auras that were far stronger than the creatures attacking them outside. But he did not enter. He did not investigate. Caroline was still his priority.
After what felt like a long and brutal ascent, the cursed clouds finally appeared directly above them.

They were thick, dark, and filled with green-purple lightning, but Max did not slow down. The golden shield around him brightened once more, and with Nancy following closely, he flew straight into the cloud layer.

The moment they entered, visibility dropped sharply. Everything around them became misty and distorted, and strange whispers echoed in their ears, sometimes sounding like children laughing, sometimes like old women chanting, and sometimes like someone calling their names from far away.
The cursed clouds tried to confuse their senses, but Max’s gaze remained cold and steady.
Golden light surged again.
The whispers were burned away.
The mist split open.
Max and Nancy broke through the cloud layer.
The moment they emerged above the clouds, the world changed.
The top of the Witch God Tree was not a simple treetop.
It was an entire world suspended above the sky.

Massive branches stretched outward in every direction like mountain ranges, thick enough to hold forests, rivers, ruined temples, broken towers, and valleys between them. Countless leaves, each one the size of a small house, grew across the highest branches, but their colors were strange.

Some were pale silver, some were dark purple, some were black with glowing green veins, and some looked completely transparent, reflecting faint scenes that did not seem to belong to the present. Between the branches hung streams of mist that flowed like waterfalls, pouring downward into the clouds below, while above them, the sky was neither day nor night.
It was a dim, violet expanse filled with slow-moving stars that seemed too close, as if someone could touch them by reaching upward.
At the very center of the treetop was Witch God Valley.

The valley was formed between three colossal branches that curved inward like the fingers of an ancient hand. Their surfaces joined together to create a vast basin filled with cursed mist, black grass, twisted stone pillars, and rivers of dark green liquid that flowed without sound.

Strange ruins were scattered throughout the valley, some built from bone-white stone, some carved directly into the living wood, and some floating slightly above the ground as if gravity had forgotten them. In the deepest part of the valley, a huge broken statue stood half-buried in the mist.

The statue seemed to depict a woman with six arms, a crown of branches, and eyes covered by a veil, but its face was cracked beyond recognition, and from those cracks, faint green light leaked out like the glow of something still alive inside.
Max and Nancy hovered above the edge of the valley, looking down at the scene before them.
Even Max could feel that this place was dangerous.

The air here did not simply carry cursed energy. It carried an old, decayed divinity, a power that had survived countless years and had twisted into something neither holy nor demonic. The mist below moved strangely, sometimes forming faces, sometimes forming hands, and sometimes opening like mouths before closing again.
The branches beneath the valley pulsed faintly, as if the Witch God Tree itself was breathing through this place.
Nancy’s expression became extremely solemn.
"This is Witch God Valley," she said quietly. "The highest and most dangerous region of the Witch God Tree."
Max’s eyes swept across the valley, and his senses spread outward as far as they could go, searching for traces of Caroline, Seraphine, Fin, or anyone connected to the second faction.
The golden shield around them slowly faded, but the light in Max’s eyes became sharper.
"So this is where they fled," he said.
Nancy nodded. "Yes. If Caroline and the others are still alive, they should be somewhere inside."
Max looked toward the depths of the cursed valley, where the broken statue stood beneath the violet sky and the mist twisted like living shadows.
"Then we go in."
His voice was calm, but the killing intent beneath it was unmistakable.
Without waiting any longer, Max descended toward Witch God Valley, and Nancy followed closely behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1752: Cursed Roots!
paragraphs: Max and Nancy had barely descended into the outer region of Witch God Valley when the cursed mist around them began to move strangely, and although the valley looked silent from above, the moment their feet touched the dark wooden ground formed by the highest branches of the Witch God Tree, Max immediately sensed that something hidden beneath the surface had awakened.

The black grass swayed without wind, the mist crawling across the ground gathered into thin streams, and the twisted stone pillars scattered throughout the valley released faint green light as if they were silently watching the two intruders enter a forbidden place.
Nancy’s expression changed slightly. "Be careful."
Before her words fully faded, the ground beneath them exploded.
Boom!

Countless tree roots burst out from beneath the surface, thick, black, and covered in glowing green veins that pulsed like cursed blood. They did not rise slowly like ordinary roots. They shot out like spears, whips, and serpents at the same time, tearing through the dark wooden ground and rushing toward Max and Nancy from every direction.

Some roots came from beneath their feet, some twisted down from the branches above, some emerged from the mist, and some even extended from the nearby stone pillars as if the entire valley had become a living cage trying to devour them.
Max’s eyes turned cold.
Dragonheart appeared in his hand in an instant, and the Severing Sword Concept erupted from his blade like an invisible edge capable of cutting apart anything in its path.

He swung his sword once, and a sharp sword light swept outward, severing dozens of roots before they could reach him. The cut roots fell to the ground and twitched violently, leaking dark green liquid that hissed against the wooden surface like poison burning through flesh.
But more roots came.
Far more.
Max slashed again.
Then again.

Each sword strike released a terrifying severing force, and every time Dragonheart moved, hundreds of roots were cleanly cut apart. Some roots were sliced into several pieces before they could even fully emerge from the ground, while others were split lengthwise as the sword light passed through them.
The Severing Sword Concept was extremely effective against them, and under Max’s sword, even these cursed roots could not resist for long.
However, their number was simply too high.
The entire valley seemed to be producing them endlessly.
The roots did not care how many were cut down. They continued rushing forward without pause, layering over one another until the air around Max and Nancy became filled with black, twisting lines.
From a distance, it looked as if the Witch God Tree itself had opened countless veins and sent them all to swallow the intruders alive.
Max’s expression remained calm.

No matter how many roots came toward him, he cut them down with cold precision. His sword moved so quickly that it left behind only faint afterimages, and every slash carried the eerie sharpness of the Severing Sword Concept.

Roots came from above, and he cut them before they descended. Roots came from beneath, and he split them as they broke through the ground. Roots tried to wrap around his arms and legs, but they were severed before they could tighten.
Even when dozens attacked him from blind spots, Max turned slightly and swept Dragonheart around his body, forming a circular sword light that shredded everything approaching him.
Nancy, however, was having a much harder time.

She was strong, and her reaction was not slow. The moment the roots attacked, she drew her sword and released her light concept together with her Death Wind concept. Pale silver light flashed around her blade, while gray-green Death Wind wrapped around the edge, and every strike she made cut several roots apart while also corroding the vitality hidden inside them.

When the roots came too densely, she shifted her figure through the mist, dodging between attacks with elegant movements, then slashed out with crescent-shaped waves of light and death wind that tore apart the roots chasing her.
For a while, she managed to hold on.
Her sword cut down one group of roots.
Her Death Wind withered another.
Her light concept burned through several more.

But the roots were not attacking like ordinary enemies. They came endlessly, without fear, without hesitation, and without any sense of pain. Every time Nancy cut down ten, thirty more rushed from another direction.
Every time she dodged one wave, another rose beneath her feet.
Gradually, the space around her became smaller and smaller, and even her movements began to slow under the overwhelming pressure.
"Nancy!" Max called out coldly as he noticed her situation.
"I can handle it!" Nancy replied, but even as she spoke, several roots tore through the mist behind her and wrapped around her left arm.
She severed them instantly with Death Wind, but that moment of delay was enough.
More roots rushed in.
One wrapped around her waist.
Another caught her ankle.
Three more coiled around her sword arm.

Nancy’s eyes sharpened, and she released a burst of light from her body, burning several roots apart, but the surrounding roots immediately layered over her again. Their number was too great, and before she could fully break free, dozens of thick roots surged from all sides and swallowed her figure completely.
In the next instant, Nancy disappeared inside a massive cocoon of black roots.
Max’s eyes turned icy.
"Damn."
His body moved instantly.
The roots tried to block him, but Max rushed forward like a sharp black shadow, Dragonheart cutting apart everything in his path.
At the same time, black flames burst into his right hand blazing with devouring intent.
Max thrust his hand forward.
Boom!
Black flames exploded across the root cocoon.

The moment the cursed roots touched the black flames, they burned violently. Their green veins flared, their surfaces cracked, and the dark liquid inside them evaporated into foul smoke before the roots could even struggle. Unlike sword cuts, which only severed them, the black flames destroyed them completely, turning them into ash and erasing the cursed vitality that allowed them to keep moving.
In only a breath, the root cocoon was burned open.
Max reached inside, grabbed Nancy by the arm, and pulled her out.

Nancy’s face was slightly pale, and several marks had been left on her arms and waist where the roots had tried to bind her, but she was still conscious. The moment Max pulled her free, she coughed once and quickly steadied herself beside him.
"Are you injured?" Max asked without looking away from the roots still rushing toward them.
"Not seriously," Nancy said, though her breathing was a little unstable. "Those roots were trying to drain my energy."
Max’s gaze became colder.
"Then stay close."
The black flames around his body erupted again.

This time, Max did not use them as a simple attack. He spread them outward, forming a sphere of black flames around both himself and Nancy. The flame sphere burned silently at first, then began rotating slowly, its surface rippling like a dark sun wrapped around them.
The cursed roots continued attacking from every direction, but the moment they touched the sphere of black flames, they were burned into nothingness before they could even exert force.
Hiss! Hiss! Hiss!
One root after another vanished.
The roots came from above and turned to ash.
They came from below and were burned away.
They rushed through the mist in waves, but none could pass through the black flame sphere.

The entire area around Max and Nancy became filled with the smell of burning cursed wood, and the ground beneath them trembled as the Witch God Tree seemed to react angrily to the destruction of its roots.
More and more roots rose from the valley, but it no longer mattered. The black flames devoured all of them, leaving behind only drifting ash and shrinking trails of green smoke.
Nancy stood inside the sphere of black flames, looking at Max’s back with a complicated expression.

She had been trapped only for a moment, but she knew very well that if Max had acted even a little slower, those roots might have drained her power or dragged her deeper into the valley. This place was far more dangerous than she had expected, and they had only just entered the outer region.
Max looked at the endless roots burning outside the flame sphere and narrowed his eyes.
"So the valley itself is trying to stop us."
Nancy took a slow breath and nodded. "Witch God Valley is alive in a strange way. The deeper we go, the worse it will become."
Max’s expression remained cold.
"We have to be serious here."
The black flame sphere expanded slightly, and every root near them was erased at once.

With Nancy close beside him, Max stepped forward into the mist, surrounded by the rotating sphere of black flames, while the cursed roots of the Witch God Tree continued rushing toward them only to be burned into nothingness the moment they touched his protection.

After another five minutes, these cursed tree roots stopped attacking them. Inside the black flaming sphere, Max didn’t underestimate the cursed roots and kept the sphere up and continued walking forward.
They walked for an hour before the region of cursed roots slowly disappeared into nothingness. Only then Max let go of the sphere of black flames.

chapters.title: Chapter 1753: Jessica and Lumine!
paragraphs: Just when Max and Nancy came out of the cursed root region, the black flame sphere around them slowly shrank back into Max’s body, and the scorched smell of burned roots faded behind them as they entered a denser part of Witch God Valley.

The mist here was thicker than before, and the trees growing across the valley were twisted and pale, their branches curling downward like claws, while faint green runes appeared and disappeared across their bark as if something ancient was breathing through them.

Max had only taken a few steps forward when his eyes suddenly narrowed, and the spatial senses of his Dimensional Sovereign Body spread outward like invisible ripples, passing through the mist, the trees, and the broken ruins ahead.
"Battles are happening ahead of us," Max said calmly.
Nancy immediately became alert. "Battles?"
Max looked into the distance. "There are some elves there, and even some demons."
Nancy’s expression changed slightly. "Demons inside Witch God Valley?"
Max glanced at her. "Is that unusual?"
"Not impossible," Nancy said with a frown. "But if demons are involved with the elves here, then the situation might be worse than we thought."
Max’s gaze became colder. "Then let us go and see."

With that, his figure moved toward the distance ahead, and Nancy followed closely behind him. The two of them passed through the cursed mist like streaks of light, avoiding the twisted trees, broken stone altars, and strange pools of dark green liquid scattered throughout the area.
Soon, faint sounds of battle entered their ears. Sword clashes, demonic roars, angry shouts, and the tremble of energy spreading through the forest all became clearer with every passing breath.
In an area enclosed by several dead white trees, a group of elves were surrounded by demons and elves.

The surrounded group numbered only five individuals, and although each of them looked injured, they were still standing back to back with their weapons raised. Their clothes were torn in many places, traces of blood marked their arms and shoulders, and their breathing was heavy, but the determination in their eyes had not faded.

These five elves belonged to the third faction, the faction that had once been led by Max’s mother, Divine Queen Caelira, and from the hatred burning in their eyes, it was obvious that surrendering was not something they would ever accept.

The ones surrounding them, however, numbered more than twenty. Some were elves with golden and pale-green hair, dressed in bright armor marked by the symbol of the second faction, while the others were demons with black horns, dark scales, and cruel smiles on their faces.
Their mixed formation looked extremely strange, yet it was clear that they had joined hands for one purpose.

They were hunting the third faction members, and if they succeeded, the members of the third faction and the others would be sent back to the Elf Prison, where torture, humiliation, and endless darkness were waiting for them once again.
Among the five surrounded elves, the leader was a blue-haired female elf.
Her long blue hair fell down her back like flowing water, but around the back of her forehead, faint specks of gold shone through the strands, making her hair look cool and noble at the same time.

Her eyes were sharp, her face was pale from exhaustion, and one side of her shoulder was stained with blood, but her sword remained steady as she pointed it toward the golden-haired female elf standing among the encircling group.
"How shameless can you be, Lumine?" the blue-haired female elf sneered. Her name was Jessica.
The golden-haired female elf smiled faintly.
Her name was Lumine.

She was beautiful, with long golden hair, clear green eyes, and a graceful appearance that made her seem gentle at first glance, but the coldness hidden in her smile destroyed that illusion completely.

She stood calmly among demons and elves as if there was nothing wrong with the scene at all, and when Jessica’s sword pointed at her, she did not show even the slightest anger. Instead, her expression only became more amused.
Jessica’s eyes burned with disgust. "To join hands with demons, the mortal enemies of the elf race, Lumine, you and your faction have truly fallen too low!"
The other four third faction elves beside Jessica also looked furious.
For elves, demons were not merely enemies competing inside the Cosmic Ascension Conference. They were old enemies of their race, creatures whose history was soaked in blood and hatred.

Even though the second faction had already committed unforgivable crimes by imprisoning and torturing the third faction members, openly cooperating with demons still crossed a line that made Jessica feel nothing but disgust.
Lumine lightly brushed a strand of golden hair behind her ear, her smile calm and cold. "Jessica, you are still as naïve as ever."
Jessica’s eyes narrowed. "Naïve?"

"Yes," Lumine said softly. "You still speak as though honor matters. You still speak as though race matters. You still speak as though the third faction has the right to stand proudly after losing everything."
Jessica’s grip on her sword tightened. "The third faction lost everything because of people like you."

Lumine’s smile deepened. "No. The third faction lost everything because Caelira abandoned her duty, abandoned her bloodline, abandoned the elf race, and chose a human man over the throne that should have ruled us all."
The moment Caelira’s name was spoken, Jessica’s eyes became colder.
"Do not speak her name with that filthy mouth," Jessica said.
Lumine laughed lightly. "Even now, you still defend her. How touching."

Jessica’s voice trembled with anger. "Divine Queen Caelira was the rightful leader of our faction. She protected us when your faction schemed in the dark, and even after she left, you were still so afraid of her shadow that you imprisoned everyone connected to her."

Lumine’s eyes flashed with cruelty. "Afraid? No, Jessica. We were cautious. Your faction still carried loyalty toward Caelira. Your faction still believed she would return one day. Your faction still treated her bloodline as sacred. So yes, you were imprisoned. You were tortured. You were broken. And after this conference ends, those of you who survive will be dragged back to the Elf Prison and broken again until no one dares to speak Caelira’s name with reverence."
The four elves around Jessica clenched their weapons, and one of them shouted, "You will pay for what you did to our people!"
Lumine looked at him with cold amusement. "Will I?"
Jessica’s sword released a blue light mixed with faint gold, and her killing intent sharpened. "You hunted us all the way into Witch God Valley just to send us back to that prison?"

"Of course," Lumine said without hesitation. "Do you think we would allow the remnants of the third faction to roam freely inside the Cosmic Ascension Conference? This world gives everyone opportunities. Treasures, inheritances, legacies, bloodline resources, and perhaps even chances to contact outside forces. If your people grow strong here, you might become troublesome after leaving. So we will capture you now, send you back, and make sure your faction remains buried where it belongs."
Her expression turned cruel. "As for Caroline, I believe Seraphine and Fin should have taken care of her by now."
"You will regret this." Jessica said coldly as she heard about Caroline.
The demon leader chuckled and lifted his axe from his shoulder. "Enough talking. Are we killing them or capturing them? The longer we delay, the more people might arrive."
Lumine looked at Jessica and the four elves beside her.
There was no hesitation in her eyes now.
"Capture Jessica if possible," Lumine said coldly. "She has information about Caroline. As for the others, cripple them first. If they resist too much, kill them."
Jessica’s group immediately became tense.
The demons grinned.
The elves of Lumine’s side raised their weapons.
But just as the surrounding group prepared to attack, a faint voice suddenly came from beyond the mist.
"Interesting."
Everyone froze.
Lumine’s eyes narrowed.
Jessica turned sharply toward the direction of the voice.
The demon leader’s grip tightened around his axe.

From between the twisted white trees, Max and Nancy slowly walked out. Max’s expression was calm, but his eyes swept across the demons and the second faction elves with a coldness that made the air around him feel heavier, while Nancy, standing beside him, immediately recognized the faction marks on both sides and understood the situation at once.
Max glanced at Jessica and the four injured elves, then looked toward Nancy.
"They are from my mother’s faction?"

Nancy nodded with a serious expression. "Yes. Jessica and the ones beside her belong to the third faction, the faction once led by Divine Queen Caelira. Lumine and those elves surrounding them are from the second faction."
Max’s gaze moved toward Lumine, then toward the demon leader.
His smile became faint and cold.
"So the second faction is working with demons to hunt my mother’s people."
The moment those words fell, Jessica’s eyes widened slightly.
Lumine’s expression changed.
Nancy looked at Max’s back, and for some reason, she felt the air around him becoming colder than the cursed mist of Witch God Valley itself.
Max took one step forward.
"Good," he said softly. "This saves me the trouble of looking for you."

chapters.title: Chapter 1754: Caelira’s Son?!
paragraphs: "Did you just say ’my mother’..." Lumine’s expression changed for the first time, and the cold amusement in her eyes was replaced by genuine shock as she stared at Max with disbelief. "Are you Caelira’s son?"
The five surrounded elves behind Jessica also froze when they heard those words.

Jessica’s eyes widened slightly, and the sword in her hand trembled for a brief moment. Caelira’s son. Those three words struck her heart with a force greater than any attack Lumine had launched against them.

She had heard rumors from the older members of the third faction, stories whispered in the darkness of the Elf Prison, stories about Divine Queen Caelira leaving the elf race, marrying a human, and giving birth to a child who should have been the hope of their bloodline.

But most of them had believed that child had died long ago during the attack arranged by the second faction. To see a young man standing here now, speaking of Caelira as his mother, felt so impossible that Jessica almost forgot the danger surrounding them.
Max looked at Lumine, his eyes cold and calm.
"It does not matter, does it?"
Lumine stared at him for a moment, then suddenly laughed.
"True," she said, and her smile became cold again. "It truly does not matter whether you are Caelira’s son or not. If you are, then killing you here will only make this more meaningful."
Her gaze shifted toward the leading demon.
"Arnold, kill him!"
The demon leader grinned.

Arnold’s already large body suddenly expanded further. His muscles swelled beneath his rough black armor, his demonic veins bulged across his arms, and a brutal aura erupted from him like a raging beast breaking free from its chains.
The ground beneath his feet cracked as he stepped forward, and in the next instant, he shot toward Max with terrifying speed, raising one massive fist and smashing it toward Max’s head.
"Watch out!" Jessica shouted instinctively.

In her eyes, Max’s cultivation aura seemed to be only at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm. Arnold, however, was at the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm, and although demons were often crude, their physical strength was terrifying among beings of the same realm.
Even an elf at the same level would not dare to casually take Arnold’s fist head-on, much less someone who seemed to be a full major realm lower.
The fist arrived before Max.
Boom!
The wind exploded outward.
The ground behind Max cracked from the pressure alone, and several nearby trees bent backward violently from the force of Arnold’s punch.
But Max did not move.
He merely raised one finger.
Arnold’s massive fist stopped.
It was not slowed down.
It was not deflected.
It was stopped completely.
Max’s single finger pressed against the center of Arnold’s fist, and the terrifying demonic force that should have crushed his head was blocked as if it had struck an immovable divine wall.

The shockwave spread in all directions, tearing through the mist and shaking the nearby cursed trees, but Max stood there without taking even half a step back. His expression remained calm, and the finger he used to block the attack did not tremble at all.
The entire area fell silent.
Jessica stared at the scene with wide eyes.
Lumine’s expression stiffened.
Even the demons behind Arnold stopped smiling.
Arnold himself looked at his fist, then at Max’s finger, and for the first time, disbelief appeared in his eyes.
Max looked at him indifferently.
"Is that supposed to hurt me?"
Those words were quiet, but they landed like a slap across Arnold’s face.
The demon leader’s eyes instantly turned bloodshot with anger.
"You arrogant brat!"

Arnold roared and swung his other fist toward Max’s chest. This punch was even stronger than the first. Demonic energy wrapped around his arm, and a dark red light gathered over his knuckles as he tried to crush Max with brute force. The air screamed beneath the punch, and the ground around them sank from the pressure.
Max raised his other hand.
Another finger moved.
Boom!
Arnold’s second fist stopped as well.
This time, Max blocked it with another finger.
The two massive fists remained frozen in front of him, each one pressed against a single finger, and the image was so absurd that even Lumine could not immediately react.

Arnold was a peak Law Manifestation Realm demon known for his physical strength, yet Max was stopping both of his fists with two fingers, standing there with the same calm expression as though Arnold’s full-powered attack was nothing more than a child throwing a tantrum.
Max looked into Arnold’s furious eyes and spoke calmly.
"You are weak."
Arnold’s face twisted with rage.
Max’s gaze became colder.
"Let me show you what true strength is."
The moment those words fell, the air around Max changed.
A deep, ancient, and terrifying draconic pressure erupted from his body.
One thousand Draconic Essences.
Two thousand.
Three thousand.
Four thousand.
Five thousand.

The full power of five thousand Draconic Essences surged out at once, and the entire region seemed to tremble beneath the awakening of a primordial dragon. The cursed mist around Max was blasted apart. The trees nearby groaned as if they were about to be uprooted.

The ground beneath his feet shattered instantly, cracks spreading outward like a spiderweb through the dark wooden surface of the Witch God Valley. The air became heavy, violent, and suffocating, as though an ancient dragon had opened its eyes and looked down upon everything in front of it.
Arnold’s expression changed completely.

The overwhelming demonic arrogance in his eyes vanished, replaced by shock and instinctive fear. His body reacted before his mind could. Even though his fists were still pressed against Max’s fingers, his legs trembled, and he was forced to take a step back under the crushing weight of Max’s aura.
A peak Law Manifestation Realm demon had been forced back by aura alone.
Jessica felt her heart shake violently.
"This power..." she whispered.

Lumine’s face also darkened, and her eyes became filled with disbelief. This was not the power of a normal peak Law Refinement Realm cultivator. This was not even close. The pressure Max released had completely broken common sense, and for a brief instant, she felt as if she was not looking at a human, but at a beast that had worn human skin.
Max smiled faintly.
He lifted one finger.
All five thousand Draconic Essences gathered toward that finger.

The golden-black draconic power condensed rapidly, becoming denser and sharper with every passing breath. The space around his fingertip distorted slightly, and the aura gathered there felt heavier than a mountain, fiercer than a storm, and more destructive than any ordinary technique Arnold had ever faced. The demon leader’s instincts screamed at him that he absolutely could not take this attack head-on.
Arnold roared and retreated half a step, then pulled out a huge axe from behind him.

The axe was enormous, almost as tall as his body, forged from dark metal and covered in demonic runes. The moment he held it in both hands, dark red energy flowed across its blade, forming several layers of defensive power. Arnold poured all his strength into the weapon and placed it in front of himself like a shield.
"You think one finger can kill me?" Arnold roared.

chapters.title: Chapter 1755: A Flick of Fingers!
paragraphs: Max’s expression remained calm.
Then he flicked his finger.
A tiny burst of condensed draconic force shot forward.
It did not look grand.
It did not look like a divine ability.
It was only a finger flick.
But the moment that force struck Arnold’s axe, the huge demonic weapon exploded.
Crack!
The first sound was small.
Then countless cracks spread across the axe.

In the next instant, the entire weapon shattered into fragments, and the condensed force did not slow down at all. It passed through the broken axe, struck Arnold’s chest, and pierced through him with irresistible power.
Arnold’s eyes widened.
His roar stopped.
His massive body froze in place.

For a single breath, he seemed unable to understand what had happened. Then his chest cracked open with golden-black light, and his entire body began breaking apart from the point of impact. The cracks spread across his armor, his muscles, his horns, and his face, and before he could scream, his body shattered completely.
The leading demon Arnold was destroyed.
His body turned into golden fragments of Killing Points that scattered through the air like broken stars before flying toward Max.
The entire battlefield fell into absolute silence.
The demons who had been laughing a moment ago now looked as if their throats had been seized by invisible hands.
The second faction elves stared at Max with pale faces.
Jessica and the other third faction elves stood frozen, unable to reconcile the person before them with the cultivation aura they had sensed earlier.
Max lowered his hand slowly as the fragments of Killing Points entered his body.
"Everyone attack!"
Seeing Arnold being killed in such a terrifying way, Lumine finally felt fear crawl into her heart, and the calm arrogance she had shown earlier cracked apart almost instantly.
Arnold had been a peak Law Manifestation Realm demon with monstrous physical strength, yet Max had blocked his punches with two fingers and destroyed him with nothing more than a flick of his finger.
This was not something that could be explained by ordinary talent, nor was it something that could be ignored by pretending Max was only at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.

The young man standing in front of her was dangerous, far more dangerous than she had expected, and if they allowed him to take the initiative again, none of them might be able to leave Witch God Valley alive.
At Lumine’s command, all the remaining second faction elves and demons moved at once.
No one dared to underestimate Max anymore.

The demons roared and released their demonic energy without holding anything back. Some charged straight toward him with heavy weapons, their axes, hammers, and bone blades wrapped in dark red killing light, while others circled to his back and sides, trying to strike from blind spots.

The second faction elves also attacked together. Golden light, green wind, pale sword aura, and sharp wood-element arrows tore through the cursed mist as they launched techniques from every direction, coordinating with the demons to seal off all possible routes of escape.

Some aimed at Max’s head, some aimed at his heart, some tried to bind his legs with glowing vines, and some released restraining light toward his arms, clearly intending to limit his movement before killing him.
The battlefield exploded into chaos.
Jessica and the four third faction elves instinctively tightened their grips on their weapons, but before they could step forward to help, Nancy raised one hand slightly and stopped them.
"Do not interfere," Nancy said in a low voice.
Jessica looked at her in confusion and urgency. "But they are all attacking him at once."
Nancy’s eyes remained fixed on Max’s back. "That is why you should not interfere."
Jessica froze slightly.

At the center of the storm, Max looked at the attacks rushing toward him from every direction with a calm expression. The five thousand Draconic Essences still surged around his body like an invisible dragon sea, but he did not use them to crush his enemies immediately. Instead, he slowly raised his hand, and Dragonheart appeared in his grip.
The moment Dragonheart emerged, the sword hummed.

A deep sword resonance spread across the battlefield, and the weapons in the hands of several second faction elves trembled uncontrollably. Even Lumine’s sword reacted, producing a faint cry that made her expression change again.
The sword in Max’s hand was not merely powerful. It carried a natural suppression toward other swords, and the aura sleeping inside it felt ancient, noble, and dangerous.
"I would love to play with you all," Max said calmly, his eyes sweeping across the incoming elves and demons, "but I am in a hurry."
His fingers tightened around Dragonheart.
"So, you guys can die."
As he said those words, Max executed the Saint Origin Sword Art.
At the same time, his expression changed.

The faint smile on his face disappeared, and his eyes became deathly calm. Emotion left his features like water draining from a broken vessel, and the eerie aura of his Pseudo Cosmic Path spread outward once again.
The Emotion Severing Path descended upon the battlefield, silent, cold, and terrifying, turning the already cursed air of Witch God Valley into something even more suffocating.
The demons felt it first.
Their battle intent weakened.
Their roars suddenly sounded hollow.
The second faction elves felt it next.

Their killing intent, anger, fear, greed, hatred, and confidence all seemed to be touched by an invisible blade, and for a brief but fatal instant, their minds went blank. The Emotion Severing Path did not simply pressure them.
It cut away the emotions that supported their actions, leaving their attacks moving forward while their hearts lagged behind in confusion and terror.
Then the Saint Origin Sword Art erupted.
A pure and majestic sword light rose from Dragonheart, yet because it was infused with the Emotion Severing Path, that originally sacred sword light became strangely cold and absolute.

It looked like the first light born from heaven and earth, but within that light was an emotionless severing force that judged everything before it as something to be cut down. Max stepped forward once, and the entire battlefield seemed to fall under his sword.
The first slash crossed the left side.

A crescent of saintly sword light swept through the demons charging from that direction. Their dark armor, demonic weapons, thick bodies, and defensive energy were all split apart at the same time. Several demons continued running for another step before their bodies separated, their eyes still frozen in disbelief as they dissolved into golden fragments of Killing Points.
The second slash turned toward the right.

The elves attacking from that side raised their defensive light barriers, but the Saint Origin Sword Art pierced through them cleanly. The barriers broke like thin glass, their swords snapped, and their bodies were cut open before they could even cry out.
Their golden and green light techniques vanished in the air, severed from their source by Max’s Pseudo Cosmic Path.
The third slash swept behind him.

The demons and elves who had tried to attack from his blind spot were cut down together. One demon had already raised his hammer above Max’s head, while another elf had almost completed a binding formation around his feet, but neither attack landed.
The sword light passed through them silently, and their bodies collapsed into fragments before the hammer could fall or the formation could close.

chapters.title: Chapter 1756: Lumine’s shock!
paragraphs: Then Max moved faster.
Dragonheart flashed again and again.

The Saint Origin Sword Art unfolded in his hand with terrifying elegance. Every movement was smooth, precise, and filled with an ancient sword rhythm, as if Max was not fighting a group of enemies but performing a sacred execution beneath the cursed trees of Witch God Valley.
Sword light spread through the battlefield in layers, crossing, turning, rising, and descending, and every line it formed became a boundary between life and death.
The demons tried to resist with brute force.
They were cut apart.
The second faction elves tried to defend with bloodline techniques.
They were cut apart.
Some tried to retreat.
They were cut apart before they could take three steps.
Some tried to beg.
Their voices were severed before they could become words.
The Emotion Severing Path made Max’s sword merciless to a frightening degree. There was no hesitation in his strikes, no unnecessary cruelty, no rage, and no pleasure.

He simply cut down everyone who had attacked him, and because his sword carried the power to sever emotion, concept, energy, defense, and life at once, none of them could withstand even a single direct slash.
Lumine stood frozen.
Her face was pale.
Her lips parted slightly, but no sound came out.

Everything had happened too quickly. She had ordered everyone to attack because she believed numbers could at least create a chance, but the moment Max drew Dragonheart and entered that emotionless sword state, the entire battle had turned into a slaughter. No, it could not even be called a battle.

The demons and second faction elves had launched their strongest attacks, surrounded him from all sides, and tried to kill him together, yet Max had wiped them out as though they were dry leaves caught in a sword storm.
Within only a few breaths, the battlefield became quiet again.
The attacks vanished.
The roaring demons disappeared.
The second faction elves collapsed into light.

Golden fragments of Killing Points floated through the cursed mist, gathering around Max like countless sparks born from death. They streamed toward him one after another, entering his body and increasing his total once again, while Dragonheart remained lowered in his hand, its blade clean and faintly humming with the remnant power of the Saint Origin Sword Art.
Jessica and the other third faction elves stared at Max in shock.
They had thought they were about to die.
They had thought Lumine and the demons would drag them back to the Elf Prison.

But the young man who claimed a connection to Caelira had appeared, killed Arnold with one finger, and then erased the rest of the enemies with a sword art so terrifying that none of them could even understand its full depth.
Nancy’s expression was also serious.
Even though she had seen Max kill before, the Saint Origin Sword Art combined with the Emotion Severing Path still made her feel a faint chill.

This was a sword art that already carried a grand and sacred origin, yet when fused with Max’s Pseudo Cosmic Path, it became something far more terrifying. It was beautiful, but it was also absolute. It gave no mercy because mercy itself seemed to be severed before the sword even fell.
At the center of the battlefield, only Lumine remained.
She had not attacked directly, and perhaps because of that, Max had intentionally left her alive.
Her body trembled faintly as she looked around at the empty battlefield. The elves she had brought were gone. The demons she had used were gone. Arnold, her strongest helper, was gone.
The only things left around her were drifting Killing Points, scorched cursed mist, severed traces of attacks, and Max standing calmly with Dragonheart in his hand.
Max slowly turned his gaze toward her.
Lumine instinctively took a step back.
For the first time since appearing, fear completely covered her face.
Max’s emotionless expression slowly softened, but the coldness in his eyes did not disappear.

"I guess you and the others have more lives left," he said with terrifying calmness in his eyes as he looked at Lumine, whose face had already lost all color. "If you want revenge for this, then you are welcome to block me at the border of Witch God Valley down below, at the entrance of the Witch God Tree."
With that, Max’s sword flashed once more.

Lumine wanted to say something. Perhaps she wanted to curse him, perhaps she wanted to threaten him with the second faction, or perhaps she wanted to reveal something about Caroline to save herself, but before even a single word could leave her mouth, a golden line appeared on her body from the top of her head to the bottom of her feet.
Her eyes widened.
In the next instant, her body split cleanly into two.
There was no scream.
There was no resistance.

Her figure dissolved into golden fragments of Killing Points, scattering into the cursed mist before streaming toward Max together with the remaining fragments left behind by Arnold, the demons, and the second faction elves.
For a moment, the entire area glowed with golden light.

The demons had carried a decent amount of Killing Points, especially Arnold, whose strength and status among them had clearly been higher than the rest. The second faction elves had also gathered points during their hunt through Witch God Valley, and Lumine, being the leader among them, carried even more than the ordinary elves under her command. One by one, their points surged into Max’s body, causing the number beside his name to rise again.
[Participant: Max]
[Previous Killing Points: 29,000,000]
[Absorbed Killing Points from Arnold: 1,500,000]
[Absorbed Killing Points from Lumine: 1,200,000]
[Absorbed Killing Points from remaining demons and second faction elves: 1,900,000]
[Total Absorbed Killing Points: 4,600,000]
[Current Killing Points: 33,600,000]
[Rank: 7]
The notification appeared quietly, but to Jessica and the other third faction elves, those numbers felt thunderous.
Thirty-three million and six hundred thousand Killing Points.

That number was no longer something an ordinary genius could hope to touch. Even many powerful participants who had survived until now might not have gathered even a small fraction of that amount, yet Max had increased his total again after casually slaughtering a group that had nearly forced Jessica and her companions into despair.
Max glanced at the notification for only a moment before looking away.
"Only four million six hundred thousand," he said calmly. "Better than the Sword God Palace disciples, but still not much."
Jessica and the other elves stared at him in silence.
For them, that amount was already terrifying.
For Max, it was merely acceptable.

Nancy looked at him with a helpless expression, though even she could not deny that his growth in Killing Points was becoming absurdly fast. Not long ago, he had stood at twenty-two million after destroying Karo, Munro, and the demon army.

Then he had taken seven million from the Sword God Palace disciples near the neutral city. Now, after killing Arnold, Lumine, and their group, he had reached thirty-three million six hundred thousand.
At this speed, his rank in the Cosmic Ascension Ranking List would rise again soon.
Max slowly lowered Dragonheart, then turned toward Jessica and the other injured third faction elves.
"Now," he said calmly, "tell me where Caroline is."

chapters.title: Chapter 1757: Jessica’s Recognition!
paragraphs: "Are you truly Divine Queen Caelira’s son?" Jessica asked, her voice still carrying the shock of what she had just witnessed.

Even now, she could not fully recover from Max’s overwhelming display of pure strength. Arnold, Lumine, the demons, and the second faction elves had all been wiped out in front of her, and Max had done it with such terrifying ease that Jessica almost felt as if she had been watching someone from a higher world descend into Witch God Valley to pass judgment.

Yet strength alone could not prove bloodline. The Divine Queen’s name was too sacred to the third faction, and Jessica could not allow herself to believe too quickly, especially when the matter involved Caelira’s child.
Before Max could answer, Nancy stepped forward and looked at Jessica.

"He is indeed the son of Caelira," Nancy said seriously. "In fact, if I am not wrong, there should also be his elder sister somewhere out there in the Divine Realm. They managed to escape the calamity all those years ago."
Jessica heard Nancy clearly, but disbelief still remained in her eyes.

She wanted to believe it. Every member of the third faction wanted to believe that Divine Queen Caelira’s children had survived. In the darkness of the Elf Prison, many of them had whispered about that possibility to keep themselves from breaking completely
But rumors were one thing, and seeing someone appear before her, claiming that connection while standing in the middle of Witch God Valley, was something else entirely.
Max looked at her silently for a moment.

He could see the hope in her eyes, but he could also see fear, caution, and pain. These elves had suffered because of his mother. Not because Caelira had harmed them, but because they had remained loyal to her name even after she disappeared.

They had been imprisoned, tortured, hunted, and treated as remnants that needed to be erased. Jessica’s suspicion was not disrespect. It was the caution of someone who had paid too much for misplaced trust.
Max raised his hand.
"Then look carefully."
The moment those words fell, a brilliant golden light bloomed from his body.
It was not ordinary light.

It was pure, sacred, and noble, carrying a divine pressure that instantly filled the cursed forest. The green mist of Witch God Valley retreated as if burned by something holy, and the twisted trees nearby trembled faintly beneath the radiance.

Golden patterns appeared faintly across Max’s skin, flowing like ancient veins of light, while behind him, a majestic phantom of divine luminance seemed to awaken for a brief moment. It was not the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline that belonged to ordinary royal elves.
It was purer, higher, and more terrifying, as though the bloodline had evolved beyond its original limit and stepped into a realm the elf race had only dreamed of.
Jessica froze.
The four elves behind her also froze.
Their weapons slowly lowered without them realizing it.

To them, this aura was unforgettable. Even though most of them had never stood before Divine Queen Caelira at her peak, every member of the third faction had grown up hearing about the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline.

In the Elf Prison, the older captives had described its sacred pressure, its golden radiance, and the way it made loyal bloodlines feel warmth while making traitors feel fear. The light Max released now carried that same origin, that same noble root, and yet it was even stronger than the legends they had heard.
Jessica’s eyes trembled.
"This aura..." she whispered.
Her voice almost broke.
"It is truly the Heavenly Luminance bloodline."

One of the injured elves behind her fell to one knee, not because Max forced him to, but because his body reacted before his mind could. Another elf’s eyes turned red as if he had seen the return of something thought lost forever.
Jessica stared at Max with shock, hope, and confusion all mixed together.
"No," she muttered. "This is not just the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline. It feels different than Divine Queen’s bloodline."

Nancy glanced at Max, then said quietly, "His bloodline is called the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. From what Prince Elrian told him, it is a variant above Divine Queen Caelira’s original bloodline."
Jessica’s expression changed again.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline..." she repeated softly.
For a moment, she looked as if she might finally believe him completely.
But then something else appeared in her eyes.
Confusion.
Deep confusion.
She looked at Max with a frown, and the joy that had just begun rising in her heart was suddenly covered by doubt.
"That should be impossible," Jessica said.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Why?"
Jessica took a slow breath and looked at the golden light around him again, as if trying to confirm what she was seeing.
"Because from what we knew, your bloodline was taken away from you."
The moment those words left her mouth, the air around Max became colder.
Nancy’s expression also changed.
Jessica noticed their reactions, but she continued because this matter was too important to hide.

"During the calamity all those years ago, the second faction did not only attack because they wanted to destroy Divine Queen Caelira’s family. They attacked because of the bloodline you carried. We heard fragments from the guards in the Elf Prison. We heard that Caelira’s son had inherited an abnormal Heavenly Luminance bloodline, something purer than even the royal line itself."
Her voice became heavier.
"But we were also told that the bloodline was extracted from you and placed into an elf of the second faction."
Max’s eyes became deathly calm.
The golden light around him flickered once, and the pressure in the area deepened.

Jessica looked at him with uncertainty and pain in her eyes. "That is why many of us believed you had died. A child whose bloodline was forcefully taken away could not have survived easily, especially during an attack arranged by the second faction. So I do not understand."
She stepped closer, her gaze fixed on the divine golden radiance surrounding Max.
"How can you still have this bloodline?"
Nancy turned toward Max, and for a moment, even she did not know what to say.
Max remained silent.
"It is a long story," he said after a moment, shaking his head slightly. "Now that you know it is me, can you tell me where Caroline is?"
Jessica’s expression immediately became solemn.

She looked at Max for a few breaths, as if she still wanted to ask him many things about Caelira, about his survival, about his bloodline, and about the elder sister Nancy had mentioned, but she also knew that none of those questions mattered more than Caroline’s current danger.
If Caroline died or was captured by the second faction, then another pillar of the third faction would fall, and all the hope that had barely begun to rise in Jessica’s heart would be crushed again.
"Follow me," Jessica said firmly.
Then she turned toward the other four injured elves.
"Heal here," she ordered. "We will regroup once we have saved Caroline."

The four elves clearly wanted to follow, but their bodies were covered in wounds, their energy was unstable, and the battle against Lumine’s group had already pushed them close to their limit. If they forced themselves deeper into Witch God Valley in their current state, they would become a burden rather than help.
One of them clenched his teeth and said, "Jessica, be careful."
Jessica nodded. "Stay alive."
The four elves nodded with unwilling but obedient expressions.

Arnold, Lumine, the demons, and the second faction elves had all been wiped out in front of her, and Max had done it with such terrifying ease that Jessica almost felt as if she had been watching someone from a higher world descend into Witch God Valley to pass judgment.

The Divine Queen’s name was too sacred to the third faction, and Jessica could not allow herself to believe too quickly, especially when the matter involved Caelira’s child.
Before Max could answer, Nancy stepped forward and looked at Jessica.
"He is indeed the son of Caelira," Nancy said seriously.
"In fact, if I am not wrong, there should also be his elder sister somewhere out there in the Divine Realm.
They managed to escape the calamity all those years ago."
Jessica heard Nancy clearly, but disbelief still remained in her eyes.
She wanted to believe it.
Every member of the third faction wanted to believe that Divine Queen Caelira’s children had survived.
In the darkness of the Elf Prison, many of them had whispered about that possibility to keep themselves from breaking completely
But rumors were one thing, and seeing someone appear before her, claiming that connection while standing in the middle of Witch God Valley, was something else entirely.
Max looked at her silently for a moment.
He could see the hope in her eyes, but he could also see fear, caution, and pain.
These elves had suffered because of his mother.
Not because Caelira had harmed them, but because they had remained loyal to her name even after she disappeared.
They had been imprisoned, tortured, hunted, and treated as remnants that needed to be erased.
Jessica’s suspicion was not disrespect.
It was the caution of someone who had paid too much for misplaced trust.
Max raised his hand.
"Then look carefully."
The moment those words fell, a brilliant golden light bloomed from his body.
It was not ordinary light.
It was pure, sacred, and noble, carrying a divine pressure that instantly filled the cursed forest.
The green mist of Witch God Valley retreated as if burned by something holy, and the twisted trees nearby trembled faintly beneath the radiance.
Golden patterns appeared faintly across Max’s skin, flowing like ancient veins of light, while behind him, a majestic phantom of divine luminance seemed to awaken for a brief moment.
It was not the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline that belonged to ordinary royal elves.
It was purer, higher, and more terrifying, as though the bloodline had evolved beyond its original limit and stepped into a realm the elf race had only dreamed of.
Jessica froze.
The four elves behind her also froze.
Their weapons slowly lowered without them realizing it.
To them, this aura was unforgettable.
Even though most of them had never stood before Divine Queen Caelira at her peak, every member of the third faction had grown up hearing about the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline.
In the Elf Prison, the older captives had described its sacred pressure, its golden radiance, and the way it made loyal bloodlines feel warmth while making traitors feel fear.
The light Max released now carried that same origin, that same noble root, and yet it was even stronger than the legends they had heard.
Jessica’s eyes trembled.
"This aura..." she whispered.
Her voice almost broke.
"It is truly the Heavenly Luminance bloodline."
One of the injured elves behind her fell to one knee, not because Max forced him to, but because his body reacted before his mind could.
Another elf’s eyes turned red as if he had seen the return of something thought lost forever.
Jessica stared at Max with shock, hope, and confusion all mixed together.
"No," she muttered.
"This is not just the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline.
It feels different than Divine Queen’s bloodline."
Nancy glanced at Max, then said quietly, "His bloodline is called the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.
From what Prince Elrian told him, it is a variant above Divine Queen Caelira’s original bloodline."
Jessica’s expression changed again.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline..." she repeated softly.
For a moment, she looked as if she might finally believe him completely.
But then something else appeared in her eyes.
Confusion.
Deep confusion.
She looked at Max with a frown, and the joy that had just begun rising in her heart was suddenly covered by doubt.
"That should be impossible," Jessica said.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"Why?"
Jessica took a slow breath and looked at the golden light around him again, as if trying to confirm what she was seeing.
"Because from what we knew, your bloodline was taken away from you."
The moment those words left her mouth, the air around Max became colder.
Nancy’s expression also changed.
Jessica noticed their reactions, but she continued because this matter was too important to hide.
"During the calamity all those years ago, the second faction did not only attack because they wanted to destroy Divine Queen Caelira’s family.
They attacked because of the bloodline you carried.
We heard fragments from the guards in the Elf Prison.
We heard that Caelira’s son had inherited an abnormal Heavenly Luminance bloodline, something purer than even the royal line itself."
Her voice became heavier.
"But we were also told that the bloodline was extracted from you and placed into an elf of the second faction."
Max’s eyes became deathly calm.
The golden light around him flickered once, and the pressure in the area deepened.
Jessica looked at him with uncertainty and pain in her eyes.
"That is why many of us believed you had died.
A child whose bloodline was forcefully taken away could not have survived easily, especially during an attack arranged by the second faction.
So I do not understand."
She stepped closer, her gaze fixed on the divine golden radiance surrounding Max.
"How can you still have this bloodline?"
Nancy turned toward Max, and for a moment, even she did not know what to say.
Max remained silent.
"It is a long story," he said after a moment, shaking his head slightly.
"Now that you know it is me, can you tell me where Caroline is?"
Jessica’s expression immediately became solemn.

She looked at Max for a few breaths, as if she still wanted to ask him many things about Caelira, about his survival, about his bloodline, and about the elder sister Nancy had mentioned, but she also knew that none of those questions mattered more than Caroline’s current danger.
If Caroline died or was captured by the second faction, then another pillar of the third faction would fall, and all the hope that had barely begun to rise in Jessica’s heart would be crushed again.
"Follow me," Jessica said firmly.
Then she turned toward the other four injured elves.
"Heal here," she ordered.
"We will regroup once we have saved Caroline."
The four elves clearly wanted to follow, but their bodies were covered in wounds, their energy was unstable, and the battle against Lumine’s group had already pushed them close to their limit.
If they forced themselves deeper into Witch God Valley in their current state, they would become a burden rather than help.
One of them clenched his teeth and said, "Jessica, be careful."
Jessica nodded.
"Stay alive."
The four elves nodded with unwilling but obedient expressions.

chapters.title: Chapter 1758: Caroline’s Stand!
paragraphs: Without wasting another moment, Jessica turned and rushed deeper into the cursed forest. Max followed beside her, while Nancy kept pace slightly behind them, her silver eyes constantly scanning their surroundings.

The path Jessica chose was not a straight one. She led them between twisted white trees, around pools of dark green liquid, across cracked wooden ridges, and through narrow gaps between broken stone altars.
From time to time, cursed roots twitched beneath the ground as if preparing to attack again, but the lingering black flames around Max’s body forced them back before they could emerge fully.
As they moved deeper, the pressure inside Witch God Valley grew stronger.

The mist thickened until even ordinary sight became almost useless, and the air carried a strange sweetness that made the mind feel heavy. Faint voices echoed from the trees, sometimes sounding like crying elves, sometimes like laughing demons, and sometimes like someone whispering Max’s name from behind him.

Nancy frowned several times, clearly affected by the illusions, but Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body continued sensing the true path through space, while the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline within him burned quietly, keeping the cursed influence away from his mind.
Jessica glanced back once and saw Max’s calm expression.
Her heart became even more complicated.
This young man was truly Caelira’s son.

The bloodline proved it. His power proved that he was not an ordinary human. His coldness toward the second faction also proved that he already carried hatred toward the ones who had destroyed his family.

Yet the more Jessica thought about it, the more unsettled she felt. The son of Divine Queen Caelira had returned, and he had returned with strength far beyond what she could understand. Whether this was a blessing or the beginning of an even greater storm, she could not tell.
But for now, she only needed him to save Caroline.
After several minutes of high-speed movement, a violent explosion suddenly shook the forest ahead.
Boom!

A pillar of golden light rose into the sky, tearing through the cursed mist and illuminating the nearby trees. Almost immediately after, a second power descended from above, a radiant spear of judgment that carried sharp suppressive force.
Then came a third force, silent and pale, cutting through the light like an eclipse blade before vanishing again into the mist.
Jessica’s expression changed.
"We are here."
Max’s eyes sharpened.

The three of them rushed through the final layer of trees and arrived at the edge of a wide battlefield formed between several enormous branches of the Witch God Tree. The ground here was cracked and scorched everywhere, and several ancient stone pillars had already collapsed into broken pieces.

Golden light burned across one side of the battlefield, pale eclipse shadows twisted on the other, and above everything, the cursed mist churned violently as if even Witch God Valley itself was afraid to approach the battle taking place there.
At the center of the battlefield, Caroline was fighting alone.

She looked similar to Caelira in a way that made Max’s eyes turn cold instantly. Her long golden hair was disheveled, her white battle dress was stained with blood, and several deep wounds marked her arms and waist, but her back remained straight.

Her eyes shone with bright golden light, and the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline within her continued burning around her body like a sacred flame refusing to go out. She held a slender golden sword in one hand, while light gathered around her other hand, forming shields, arrows, chains, and blades that moved with graceful precision.
Facing her were two elves.
Seraphine and Fin.

Seraphine stood in the air above the battlefield, her long golden hair floating behind her, her expression cold and dignified. Her body was wrapped in radiant armor formed from light, and behind her, a vast golden path had manifested, filled with pillars, scales, chains, and countless shining eyes that looked down upon Caroline like judges sentencing a criminal.

This was her Pseudo Cosmic Path, the Radiant Judgment Path. Every time she raised her hand, beams of light descended from the path like divine punishment, suppressing Caroline’s movements, burning through her defenses, and trying to seal her bloodline power.
Fin moved differently.
He was almost silent.

His pale-gold hair and white cloak seemed to fade in and out of the mist, and around him spread a strange Pseudo Cosmic Path of dim light and shadow. The Pale Eclipse Path twisted perception, swallowed sound, and distorted distance.

One moment he was in front of Caroline, the next he appeared behind her, his sword cutting from impossible angles with pale crescent-shaped light that looked gentle but carried deadly sharpness. If Seraphine was judgment descending from above, then Fin was execution hidden in silence.
Caroline fought both of them at once.

A golden shield appeared above her, blocking Seraphine’s radiant spear, but the moment the spear shattered, Fin’s sword appeared near her back. Caroline turned instantly, releasing a burst of golden light from her body.
The light formed dozens of thin blades around her and forced Fin’s figure to fade back into the mist, but before she could breathe, Seraphine pressed one hand downward.
"Radiant Judgment, Chain of Conviction."

Golden chains descended from the path behind Seraphine and wrapped toward Caroline from all directions. Each chain carried suppressive power that targeted her bloodline directly, and the moment they approached, the golden light around Caroline’s body flickered violently. Caroline gritted her teeth and thrust her sword upward.
"Heavenly Luminance, Breaking Dawn."

A pillar of pure light erupted from her sword and shattered several chains at once, but not all of them. One chain wrapped around her left wrist, another caught her shoulder, and for a brief moment, her movements slowed.
That moment was enough.
Fin appeared behind her like a pale shadow.
His sword stabbed silently toward her heart.
Jessica’s face turned pale. "Caroline!"

Caroline’s eyes flashed, and a pair of golden wings made of light suddenly appeared behind her. She twisted her body at the last instant, causing Fin’s sword to pierce through her side instead of her heart. Blood scattered across the air, but Caroline did not cry out. She gathered light in her palm and slammed it toward Fin’s chest.
Boom!
Fin was forced back several steps, but his body dissolved into pale eclipse light before the attack could fully injure him.
Seraphine looked down at Caroline coldly.
"You are still struggling," she said. "How pointless."

Caroline pulled Fin’s sword light out of her wound with a trembling hand, and golden light immediately covered the injury to slow the bleeding. Her breathing was heavy, and her face was pale, but her eyes remained bright with defiance.
"If you want to drag me back to the Elf Prison," Caroline said coldly, "then you will have to break every bone in my body first."
Fin appeared beside Seraphine, his expression calm and indifferent. "That can be arranged."
Seraphine raised her hand again, and the Radiant Judgment Path behind her became brighter.
"Caroline, you are the last symbol that keeps those remnants loyal to Caelira. Once you are captured, the third faction will finally understand that hope is dead."
Caroline’s eyes turned colder. "You can only wish for that."

chapters.title: Chapter 1759: Max Makes His Move!
paragraphs: Seraphine’s gaze sharpened.
"Then let me prove you wrong."

The radiant path behind her trembled, and countless spears of light began forming above the battlefield. At the same time, Fin’s Pale Eclipse Path spread outward, dimming the space around Caroline and making her figure appear isolated beneath the falling judgment.
The two Pseudo Cosmic Paths pressed down at once, one suppressing her from above and the other sealing her escape routes through distorted light and shadow.
Caroline lifted her sword with both hands.

Golden light erupted from her bloodline again, but anyone could see that she was nearly at her limit. She had already been fighting for too long. Her aura was unstable, her injuries were worsening, and against Seraphine and Fin together, even her Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline could not hold forever.
Jessica’s eyes turned red with urgency. "Max, that is Caroline."
Max did not answer.
He was staring at the woman in the center of the battlefield.
Caroline.
His mother’s younger sister.
His aunt.
Someone who had been hunted, imprisoned, and tortured because of her connection to Caelira.
The golden light in Max’s eyes slowly brightened, and the temperature around him seemed to drop despite the divine radiance beginning to rise from his body.
Nancy felt the change in him and took a silent step back.
On the battlefield, Seraphine’s hand descended.
"Radiant Judgment, Thousand Spears of Exile."
Thousands of radiant spears fell toward Caroline.
Fin’s figure vanished at the same time, reappearing behind her with his sword aimed at the wound in her side.
Caroline raised her sword, ready to endure it all.
But before the attacks could land, space rippled.
Max appeared in front of her.
He did not speak.
He simply raised one hand.

A brilliant golden barrier formed before him, carrying the aura of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, and the moment the thousand radiant spears struck it, they shattered one after another like weak glass touching an unbreakable sun. At the same time, Max turned his head slightly and looked toward the empty space behind Caroline, where Fin’s blade was about to emerge.
His other hand moved.
Dragonheart flashed.
Fin’s sword strike was forced back before it could touch Caroline.
For the first time, Seraphine’s cold expression changed.
Fin also stopped moving.
Caroline stared at the figure standing before her, her exhausted eyes filled with shock.
Max did not look back yet.
His gaze remained fixed on Seraphine and Fin.
"You two," he said calmly, but his voice carried a coldness that made the entire battlefield silent, "needs to die."

"And who are you, human?" Seraphine asked with a solemn face, her eyes fixed on Max as the shattered remnants of her radiant spears faded above the battlefield. "Why are you interfering in a fight between elves?"

Unlike Lumine, Seraphine did not immediately lose her composure, but the seriousness in her gaze deepened. The golden barrier Max had raised just now had not merely blocked her attack. It had shattered the Thousand Spears of Exile with ease, and even more importantly, the aura released from that barrier felt strangely familiar to her.

It was light. It was pure. It was connected to the Heavenly Luminance bloodline, but it was not the same as Caroline’s. It was denser, higher, and far more oppressive, which made Seraphine’s heart sink with a faint unease she could not immediately explain.
Fin, however, was different.

He appeared beside Seraphine again, his pale cloak fluttering slightly in the mist, and instead of looking cautious, he laughed with open arrogance. His eyes swept over Max like he was looking at another prey that had conveniently delivered itself to them.
"Haha, who cares, Seraphine?" Fin said. "Let us kill him too. That way we will get more points. We cannot let the Divine Son and Divine Daughter take all the fun, can we?"
The moment the words Divine Son and Divine Daughter were spoken, Caroline’s expression changed slightly, but Max only glanced at Fin with calm eyes.

Caroline, who was standing behind Max, finally recovered from her shock. Her breathing was still uneven, and the wound at her side had not fully closed, but when she saw a human standing between her and Seraphine and Fin, her first reaction was not relief. It was alarm.
"You should not have interfered," Caroline said, her voice weak but firm.
Max turned his head slightly.

Caroline looked at him with a serious expression, and despite her injuries, there was still the bearing of someone who had once stood among the core of the third faction. "I do not know who you are, and I thank you for blocking that attack, but you need to leave. These two are not ordinary elves. Seraphine and Fin are among the strongest geniuses of the second faction. Both of them have mastered Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and both of them are peak Law Manifestation Realm experts."
Her eyes moved briefly toward Seraphine’s Radiant Judgment Path and Fin’s Pale Eclipse Path, then returned to Max.
"If you stay here, you will die."

Jessica, who had arrived at the edge of the battlefield with Nancy, clenched her fists when she heard those words. She wanted to explain who Max was, but the atmosphere was too tense, and for a moment, she could not find the right time to speak.
Nancy also remained silent, but there was no worry in her eyes. She had already seen enough of Max’s strength to know that Caroline’s warning, while sincere, was based on a misunderstanding.
Max looked at Caroline for a moment.

There was blood on her battle dress, exhaustion in her eyes, and stubbornness in the way she still tried to stand straight even after being pushed to the edge by two powerful enemies. She did not know him.

She did not know he was Caelira’s son. She did not know that the human she was warning was not someone who had stumbled into this battle by accident, but someone who had crossed half of Witch God Valley to find her.
For some reason, that made Max’s gaze soften slightly.
Then he smiled.
"Do not worry," he said. "I will take care of them."
Caroline froze.
The words were spoken so casually that for a moment, she almost thought she had heard wrong.
Take care of them?
Seraphine and Fin?
Two of the second faction’s strongest young experts, both Pseudo Cosmic Path users, both peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses, and both specifically sent to capture her?

Even when she had been at her full strength, Caroline could only barely resist them by using every advantage of her Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline. She had been forced into a desperate battle, suppressed from above by the Radiant Judgment
Path and hunted from the shadows by the Pale Eclipse Path. Yet this human was smiling as if he had merely been asked to remove two stones from the road.
