chapters.title: Chapter 1769: Abyssal Witch Eye!
paragraphs: Boom!
The red beam crashed into Dragonheart.
The impact was horrifying.

A violent shockwave exploded outward, tearing the cursed mist apart and blasting Jessica, Caroline, Nancy, and the other elves backward several steps. The ground beneath Max shattered instantly, cracks spreading in all directions across the pale bark like broken glass.
His arms trembled under the force of the beam, and even though Dragonheart blocked the attack, the power behind it did not disappear. It drove into him like a collapsing mountain.
For the first time in front of them, Max was blasted away.

His body flew backward violently, smashing through a broken stone pillar and dragging a long scar across the wooden ground before he finally twisted in midair, stabbed Dragonheart into the surface beneath him, and forced himself to stop. Even then, the remaining force pushed him several more meters before the sword carved a deep trench into the ground.
The battlefield fell into stunned silence.

Jessica stared at the place where she had been standing a moment ago, her face completely pale. If Max had not moved, that red beam would have pierced through her before she even realized she was under attack.
Nancy’s eyes widened. "Max!"
Caroline’s expression changed sharply. "That attack pushed him back?"
The four third faction elves were horrified.
They had just seen Max crush Arnold with one finger, kill Lumine’s group with his sword art, and destroy Seraphine and Fin even after they released the full strength of their Pseudo Cosmic Paths.

In their minds, Max had already become an almost unstoppable existence among the younger generation. Yet now, this strange spherical eye creature had fired a single beam, and just by blocking it, Max had been blasted away.
That alone showed how terrifying the beam of red light was.
Max slowly rose from the broken ground.

His fingers tightened around Dragonheart, and a thin trail of smoke rose from the sword’s blade where the red beam had struck. His arms were slightly numb, and his eyes narrowed as he looked toward the floating eye creature blocking the entrance.
"Interesting," Max said softly.
The huge eye creature floated silently in the mist.
Its central pupil began glowing red again.
Caroline’s face turned grave. "Everyone, get behind him!"
Jessica and the others immediately moved back, no longer daring to stand near the creature’s line of sight.
Max stepped forward again, Dragonheart held in his hand, his gaze locked onto the massive blood-red pupil.
"So," he said calmly, "you are the thing guarding the way out."
"Max, do not take that thing lightly."

Caroline’s voice suddenly sounded from behind him, and although she was trying to remain calm, the seriousness in her tone made everyone’s expression change. She stared at the huge spherical eye creature floating at the entrance of Witch God Valley, and for the first time since Seraphine and Fin had fallen, clear fear appeared in her eyes.
It was not the fear of someone who had lost her courage, but the fear of someone who recognized a nightmare from old legends and understood just how dangerous it truly was.
Jessica turned toward her quickly. "Lady Caroline, you know what that creature is?"

Caroline nodded slowly, her face pale. "I have never seen it before with my own eyes, but I have heard of it. In the oldest records of the third faction, there were mentions of a cursed guardian that slept inside Witch God Valley. It was said that when the Witch God Tree was still ruled by the ancient Witch who once controlled this world, she raised a pet with the power to see through space, curse souls, and destroy anything that tried to escape her domain."
Nancy’s expression changed. "The Witch’s cursed pet?"
"Yes," Caroline said, her eyes still fixed on the giant eye. "That thing must be the guardian of Witch God Valley. It is not a normal cursed beast. It is something left behind by the Witch herself."
The moment those words were spoken, the air around the group became heavier.

The Witch who once ruled this world was not an ordinary existence. Even though countless years had passed and only broken legends remained, everything inside Witch God Valley still carried traces of her power.

The cursed roots, the living mist, the ancient ruins, the twisted trees, and even the strange pressure lingering in the valley all proved that the Witch had once reached a terrifying level. If this eye creature had truly been her pet and guardian, then it was not something they could judge by ordinary cultivation realms.

Caroline continued in a low voice, "The records called it the Abyssal Witch Eye. It was said to be born from the Witch’s own cursed blood and fed with the souls of those who betrayed her. Its eye can release a light that does not simply burn the body. It can pierce through space, lock onto life force, and carry a curse that follows the target even after the first strike misses. If you had not blocked that beam just now, Jessica might not have only died once. The curse could have damaged her remaining lives too."
Jessica’s face turned completely pale.
The four third faction elves behind her also took several steps back, their eyes filled with horror as they looked at the huge floating eye.
Nancy’s hand tightened around her sword. "No wonder the attack was so fast. It did not move like ordinary light. It cut through the distance itself."

Caroline nodded. "Exactly. That is why I said not to take it lightly. Its attacks are not something most people can dodge after seeing them. By the time the eye opens and the beam is visible, it is already too late."
Max looked at the Abyssal Witch Eye silently.

The creature floated at the entrance without moving, but the red veins across its spherical body pulsed faster than before. Its huge central pupil remained locked onto Max, as if it had recognized him as the greatest threat among the group.
Smaller eyes at the ends of its tendrils blinked one after another, and every blink released faint waves of cursed perception that swept across the battlefield, measuring the prey before it.

Caroline stepped closer despite her injuries. "Max, listen to me. That thing is guarding the exit. It may not chase us deep into the valley, but it will not let us leave easily. The Witch God Valley is not just a dangerous place. It is a cage. That creature is likely one of the reasons so many people enter and never return."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. "So we cannot avoid it."
"No," Caroline said. "At least, not if we want to leave through this entrance."
The Abyssal Witch Eye’s central pupil began glowing again.

This time, the red light gathered more slowly, but the pressure was even more terrifying than before. The space in front of it compressed inward, and the cursed mist around the entrance was pulled toward the pupil like smoke being swallowed by a vortex.
Everyone felt their skin tighten, and Jessica instinctively moved behind Max, still shaken by how close she had come to being struck earlier.
Caroline’s voice became urgent. "Max, be careful. That first attack may not have been its full power."

Caroline looked at Max’s back and said again, her voice filled with warning, "Do not fight it like a normal enemy. This thing belonged to the Witch who once ruled this world. If it still carries even a fragment of her cursed authority, then one mistake could be fatal."
Max did not look back.

A faint golden light began to gather around his body, and his Dimensional Sovereign Body spread its senses through the space before him, watching every distortion around the eye, every movement of its tendrils, and every hidden path where its attack might appear.
"Everyone stay behind me," Max said calmly.
The Abyssal Witch Eye’s pupil finally opened wider.
The red beam was about to fire again.
Max’s eyes became sharp.
"I will cut a path out."
The Abyssal Witch Eye’s huge central pupil widened, and the red light gathering inside it became even more intense than before.

This time, the creature did not release its attack immediately. The veins across its spherical body pulsed rapidly, and the smaller eyes at the ends of its tendrils all turned toward Max at once, blinking in a strange rhythm as if they were helping the main eye lock onto his position through space itself.

The cursed mist near the entrance was dragged toward the pupil and swallowed by the red glow, while the surrounding air twisted so violently that Jessica and the others felt their vision bend for a moment.
The first beam had already blasted Max away even though he had blocked it with Dragonheart, and now, as the second beam gathered, everyone could clearly feel that this attack would be stronger.
Caroline’s face turned pale. "Max, it is charging more power than before."
Max did not answer.

His eyes remained fixed on the giant eye. The Dimensional Sovereign Body spread his perception through the distorted space around the monster, and he could clearly see the path of the beam before it was even fired.

The creature was not simply aiming at him this time. The red light was spreading across several possible spatial paths, meaning that even if Max dodged, the beam could bend its route and strike the people behind him. If he wanted to protect Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the other third faction elves, then he could not simply avoid the attack.
He had to block it head-on.
Max slowly exhaled.
Then his body changed.
The first Divine Vein opened.
Vein of Origin.

A deep sound echoed from within Max’s body, like the first heartbeat of an ancient beast waking from the depth of creation. His foundation surged, his aura became heavier, and the power hidden in his flesh began to stabilize and expand as if every part of his body had been strengthened from its root. The ground beneath his feet trembled as invisible force spread through him.
The second Divine Vein opened.
Vein of Vitality.

A powerful life force erupted through his body, making his blood roar like a river of molten gold. His muscles tightened, his bones seemed to become denser, and the numbness left in his arms from blocking the first beam vanished in an instant. His entire body pulsed with vitality so overwhelming that even the cursed energy of Witch God Valley was forced away from him.
The third Divine Vein opened.
Vein of Strength.
Boom!

The wooden ground beneath Max’s feet shattered violently. Cracks spread in all directions, and the branch path at the entrance of Witch God Valley sank slightly beneath the sudden pressure released by his body. His physical strength rose to a terrifying level, and the air around his arms distorted as if his flesh alone had become capable of bearing the weight of mountains.
The fourth Divine Vein opened.
Vein of Speed.
Max’s figure blurred for a fraction of a second, not because he moved, but because the power inside his body had become too fast and too violent for the air around him to remain stable.

His senses sharpened, his reaction speed soared, and the red beam that had once seemed nearly impossible for the others to perceive now appeared completely clear within his eyes. Every ripple of space, every pulse of cursed light, and every possible route of the attack became visible to him.
Behind him, Nancy’s eyes widened.
"This is..." she whispered.

Jessica felt her breath stop. She had already seen Max display monstrous sword power, but this was different. This was not his Pseudo Cosmic Path. This was not his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.

This was pure physical strength, a terrifying body power that seemed to rise from the deepest foundation of his being. Caroline also stared at him in shock, because for a brief moment, she felt as if the person standing before the Abyssal Witch Eye was no longer simply her sister’s son, but a young dragon in human form preparing to tear apart the curse of the valley with his own hands.
The Abyssal Witch Eye fired.
A second beam of deadly red light burst from its pupil.
It was faster than the first.
Stronger than the first.

The beam tore through space with a sharp scream, and the path between the eye and Max collapsed into a burning red line. Jessica and the others could not follow it at all. They only saw the eye flash, and by the time they realized the attack had been launched, Max had already moved.
Dragonheart rose.
Max stepped forward instead of retreating.
The beam crashed into his sword.
BOOM!
The impact shook the entire entrance of Witch God Valley.
The branch path beneath him exploded into countless cracks, and waves of red light swept outward like a storm, forcing Caroline, Nancy, Jessica, and the others to retreat despite standing behind him.

However, this time, Max was not blasted away. His feet dug into the shattered ground, his arms held Dragonheart steady, and the power of his first four Divine Veins roared through his body like four divine furnaces burning at once.
The beam pushed against him.
Max pushed back.

The Abyssal Witch Eye’s huge pupil trembled, and the red light became even more violent, but Max’s body did not bend. The Vein of Origin stabilized his foundation. The Vein of Vitality kept his body from breaking under the curse pressure.
The Vein of Strength gave him the force to resist the beam head-on. The Vein of Speed allowed him to see every shift in the attack and adjust his sword at the perfect angle.
Dragonheart hummed sharply.
Max’s eyes became cold.
"You are strong," he said softly. "But not strong enough."
The Severing Sword Concept gathered along Dragonheart.
Then Max took another step forward.

The red beam, which had been pressing against his sword like a river of death, suddenly split at the center. A thin golden-black line appeared where Dragonheart touched it, and that line stretched forward through the beam as Max pushed his sword out.

The beam screamed, distorted, and tried to repair itself, but the Severing Sword Concept continued cutting through it, dividing the deadly light into two streams that flew past Max’s sides and blasted into the distant cursed trees behind him.
The trees exploded.
The ground burned.
But Max kept moving forward.
One step.
Then another.
The beam was being cut apart.

The Abyssal Witch Eye’s tendrils thrashed wildly as if it had finally sensed danger. The smaller eyes blinked faster and faster, releasing waves of curse power into the main pupil, but Max’s strength had risen too far after opening four Divine Veins.
He pushed through the beam with terrifying force, Dragonheart cutting the red light apart inch by inch until the distance between him and the giant eye rapidly shrank.

chapters.title: Chapter 1771: A Small Eye
paragraphs: Caroline stared at him in disbelief. "He is forcing his way through the beam."
The Abyssal Witch Eye released a silent pulse of fear.
Its pupil contracted.
But it was too late.
Max suddenly disappeared.

The Vein of Speed erupted, and his figure crossed the remaining distance in an instant. He appeared directly before the huge central eye, Dragonheart raised above his head, the first four Divine Veins burning through his body, and the Severing Sword Concept condensed to the edge of his blade.
The Abyssal Witch Eye tried to fire again at point-blank range.
Max slashed first.
The sword descended.
A brilliant line cut through the massive pupil.

The red light inside the eye split apart, the cursed veins across its spherical body burst one after another, and the entire creature trembled violently as the slash continued downward, severing its body from top to bottom.
The smaller eyes at the ends of its tendrils exploded into red mist, and the huge spherical body released a soundless scream that made the air tremble.
Then the Abyssal Witch Eye split in two.
For a moment, its two halves floated on either side of Max, still glowing with cursed red light.
Then they began to dissolve.

The monster’s body broke apart into dark ash, red sparks, and fragments of cursed energy that scattered into the air before being swallowed by the rules of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. A massive stream of Killing Points emerged from the remains, far brighter and denser than the fragments left by ordinary enemies, and surged toward Max.
Max landed softly at the entrance of Witch God Valley.

The first four Divine Veins slowly dimmed, but the overwhelming physical pressure around him did not disappear immediately. Cracks covered the ground beneath his feet, and Dragonheart remained lowered in his hand, its blade still releasing faint smoke from having cut through the deadly beam.
Behind him, Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the others stood frozen.

The guardian of Witch God Valley, the cursed pet of the ancient Witch, the Abyssal Witch Eye that had nearly killed Jessica with one beam and blasted Max away with its first attack, had been cut down by Max after he opened only four Divine Veins.
Max looked at the fading remains of the eye creature, then glanced toward the path beyond the entrance.
"Now," he said calmly, "we can leave."
Just as the Abyssal Witch Eye was destroyed and everyone felt a wave of relief rise in their hearts, the atmosphere at the entrance of Witch God Valley changed once again.

Jessica let out a long breath and looked at Max with eyes full of shock and admiration, while the other third faction elves could barely hide the joy on their faces after seeing the guardian of the valley finally fall.

Even Caroline, whose expression had remained heavy for so long, allowed a trace of relief to appear in her eyes. For a brief moment, it felt as if the worst part was already over. The path ahead was finally open, and with Max standing at the front, the group truly believed they could leave the cursed valley.
But just when everyone was preparing to move, a strange red-black glimmer suddenly flickered among the scattered remains of the Abyssal Witch Eye.
Max noticed it first.

His Dimensional Sovereign Body immediately sensed something subtle and sinister moving through space, but before he could react, that glimmer shot out from the dissolving ashes of the giant eye creature and appeared right beside him.

In the next instant, a small eye, almost identical in appearance to the Abyssal Witch Eye but only the size of Max’s fist, floated in the air for a brief moment before sticking itself directly onto Max’s shoulder like a living parasite.
The small eye was blood-red and black, with a vertical pupil that blinked slowly, and thin dark veins spread outward from its base the moment it attached itself to him.

It did not release an overwhelming aura like the giant guardian had, yet the sight of it was far more unsettling because of how unnatural and intimate it looked, as if the curse of the Witch itself had chosen Max as its new host.
Max’s brows furrowed instantly.
He reached out with one hand and tried to tear it off.

But the moment his fingers touched the small eye, he felt a strange resistance, as if it was not truly attached to his flesh, but to something deeper. It looked like it was sitting on his shoulder, yet when he tried to grab it, the eye blurred strangely and remained exactly where it was, neither falling away nor allowing itself to be held properly.
Jessica’s expression changed. "What is that?"
Nancy’s face became serious. "It came from the remains of the guardian."

Max’s eyes turned colder. Without hesitation, he tried again. This time he used far more force, his fingers tightening with enough strength to crush stone and metal alike, but no matter how much pressure he applied, the small eye did not break. It remained attached to him, blinking slowly, as if mocking his effort.
"This thing is tough." Max’s expression darkened.
Then he activated the first four Divine Veins again.

The Vein of Origin opened first, anchoring his body with terrifying stability. The Vein of Vitality followed, flooding his flesh and blood with violent life force. The Vein of Strength awakened next, causing the ground beneath his feet to crack once again, while the Vein of Speed sharpened his reactions and made the surrounding air tremble faintly.
The moment all four Divine Veins were open, Max’s physical power rose to a terrifying level once more.
Caroline and the others immediately stepped back.

Even though he was only focusing his strength into one hand, the pressure around him was still enormous. The bark beneath his feet splintered, the air around his arm distorted visibly, and the muscles beneath his sleeve tightened with explosive force as if a dragon’s body had been compressed into human shape. Max then placed his hand over the small eye and tried to crush it directly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1772: A True Curse!
paragraphs: A violent sound rang out.
The force he released was enough to shatter boulders and crush the bodies of powerful enemies, yet the small eye did not break.
Not even a crack appeared on it.
Instead, it remained there in the same place, blinking calmly while Max’s crushing grip caused the space around it to twist.
Jessica stared in disbelief. "It did not break?"
Nancy’s eyes narrowed. "It is not a normal object."
Max’s face turned completely cold.
The first failure did not make him stop. It only made him more serious.
Max looked at the small eye in his hand and muttered. "Let’s see how tough this eye truly is..."
As he said those words, he released his grip for a brief moment, then the power in his body surged to an even more frightening degree.
This time, in addition to the first four Divine Veins, he also unleashed the full power of his five thousand Draconic Essences.
Boom!
A monstrous force erupted from Max’s body.

Golden-black draconic power burst outward like a storm awakening from the deepest abyss. The bark-covered ground around him collapsed into a web of cracks. The cursed mist in the surrounding area was blasted apart at once, and the air became so heavy that Jessica and the others felt their breathing turn difficult.

Max’s aura at this moment was far more devastating than before. The four Divine Veins had already pushed his physical strength to a shocking level, but with the addition of five thousand Draconic Essences, that strength rose into a completely different realm.
His body looked as though it was wrapped in the pressure of an ancient dragon.
His blood roared.
His bones hummed.
The power condensed into his arm alone was enough to make everyone present feel a chill run down their spine.

Even Caroline, who had seen Max destroy Seraphine, Fin, and the Abyssal Witch Eye, could not help but feel shaken at this moment. If Max had used this level of force against an ordinary enemy, that enemy would likely have been obliterated before even understanding what had struck them.
Max’s hand closed around the small eye again.
This time, the force he released was devastating.

The sound of compression shook the area, and the bark beneath him sank lower under the pressure. The surrounding air folded inward toward his fist, and the violent force generated by his grip caused faint cracks to appear in space itself.

The mixture of the four Divine Veins and five thousand Draconic Essences had brought his raw physical strength to an absurd level, one so terrifying that even Nancy felt that if she stood too close, she might be injured by the pressure alone.
Yet even then, the small eye did not break.
It did not shatter.
It simply remained attached to him, unchanged, its tiny vertical pupil staring outward with a calm and eerie stillness that made it look less like a creature and more like a curse given shape.
Max slowly loosened his grip.
For the first time since the small eye had attached itself to him, a real frown appeared on his face.

He had even expected it to possess some strange defensive property because of its connection to the Abyssal Witch Eye. But to endure the full force of four Divine Veins and five thousand Draconic Essences without suffering the slightest damage was something else entirely.
Caroline looked at the small eye carefully, and the relief that had briefly appeared on her face vanished completely.
Her expression became solemn and uneasy.
"Max," she said slowly, "stop for a moment."
Max turned toward her.

Caroline stepped closer, though she still kept a cautious distance from the attached eye. Her eyes remained fixed on the small blood-red pupil, and the more she observed it, the more troubled she looked.
"This may not be something you can destroy with brute force," she said quietly.
Jessica frowned. "What do you mean?"
Caroline took a slow breath. "I think this may be some sort of the Witch’s curse."
The words made everyone’s expression change.
Nancy’s eyes sharpened. "A curse?"

Caroline nodded. "The giant guardian was not just a beast. It was the cursed pet of the Witch who once ruled this world. If that creature was truly linked to her authority, then this small eye might not be a living remnant in the normal sense. It could be a curse mark, a tracking brand, or a binding seal left behind by the Witch herself. That would explain why it cannot be crushed even with such overwhelming force. You are not trying to destroy ordinary flesh. You are trying to crush a curse attached to your existence."
Max looked at the eye again, his expression turning darker.
The little eye blinked once, slowly and silently, as if it was confirming Caroline’s words.

Caroline continued in a grim tone, "If I am right, then destroying the guardian may have triggered this. Perhaps it marks the one who killed it. Perhaps it allows the deeper curses of Witch God Valley to recognize you. Or perhaps it is something even worse."
Jessica swallowed hard. "Worse?"

Caroline nodded faintly. "The Witch’s curses were feared for a reason. Some mark the body. Some cling to the soul. Some make the cursed person easier to find, easier to track, or easier to drag into illusion and death. We cannot treat this lightly."
For a moment, silence fell over the entrance of Witch God Valley.

Max stood there with the small eye still attached to him, while the remnants of his power slowly settled back down. The first four Divine Veins dimmed, and the raging pressure of his five thousand Draconic Essences receded, yet the little eye remained exactly where it was, unchanged and eerily calm.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
"So it is a curse."
Caroline gave a slow nod. "Most likely."
Max looked toward the path beyond the entrance, then back at the eye attached to him.
His voice turned calm again, though the coldness in it made everyone still their breath.
"Fine," he said. "If it is a curse, then we will deal with it later."
He then looked at Caroline.
"But first, we leave this place."
The others nodded, though the unease in their eyes remained.

Even Caroline, who had seen Max destroy Seraphine, Fin, and the Abyssal Witch Eye, could not help but feel shaken at this moment.
If Max had used this level of force against an ordinary enemy, that enemy would likely have been obliterated before even understanding what had struck them.
Max’s hand closed around the small eye again.
This time, the force he released was devastating.
The sound of compression shook the area, and the bark beneath him sank lower under the pressure.
The surrounding air folded inward toward his fist, and the violent force generated by his grip caused faint cracks to appear in space itself.

The mixture of the four Divine Veins and five thousand Draconic Essences had brought his raw physical strength to an absurd level, one so terrifying that even Nancy felt that if she stood too close, she might be injured by the pressure alone.
Yet even then, the small eye did not break.
It did not shatter.
It simply remained attached to him, unchanged, its tiny vertical pupil staring outward with a calm and eerie stillness that made it look less like a creature and more like a curse given shape.
Max slowly loosened his grip.
For the first time since the small eye had attached itself to him, a real frown appeared on his face.
He had even expected it to possess some strange defensive property because of its connection to the Abyssal Witch Eye.
But to endure the full force of four Divine Veins and five thousand Draconic Essences without suffering the slightest damage was something else entirely.
Caroline looked at the small eye carefully, and the relief that had briefly appeared on her face vanished completely.
Her expression became solemn and uneasy.
"Max," she said slowly, "stop for a moment."
Max turned toward her.
Caroline stepped closer, though she still kept a cautious distance from the attached eye.
Her eyes remained fixed on the small blood-red pupil, and the more she observed it, the more troubled she looked.
"This may not be something you can destroy with brute force," she said quietly.
Jessica frowned.
"What do you mean?"
Caroline took a slow breath.
"I think this may be some sort of the Witch’s curse."
The words made everyone’s expression change.
Nancy’s eyes sharpened.
"A curse?"
Caroline nodded.
"The giant guardian was not just a beast.
It was the cursed pet of the Witch who once ruled this world.
If that creature was truly linked to her authority, then this small eye might not be a living remnant in the normal sense.
It could be a curse mark, a tracking brand, or a binding seal left behind by the Witch herself.
That would explain why it cannot be crushed even with such overwhelming force.
You are not trying to destroy ordinary flesh.
You are trying to crush a curse attached to your existence."
Max looked at the eye again, his expression turning darker.
The little eye blinked once, slowly and silently, as if it was confirming Caroline’s words.
Caroline continued in a grim tone, "If I am right, then destroying the guardian may have triggered this.
Perhaps it marks the one who killed it.
Perhaps it allows the deeper curses of Witch God Valley to recognize you.
Or perhaps it is something even worse."
Jessica swallowed hard.
"Worse?"
Caroline nodded faintly.
"The Witch’s curses were feared for a reason.
Some mark the body.
Some cling to the soul.
Some make the cursed person easier to find, easier to track, or easier to drag into illusion and death.
We cannot treat this lightly."
For a moment, silence fell over the entrance of Witch God Valley.
Max stood there with the small eye still attached to him, while the remnants of his power slowly settled back down.
The first four Divine Veins dimmed, and the raging pressure of his five thousand Draconic Essences receded, yet the little eye remained exactly where it was, unchanged and eerily calm.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
"So it is a curse."
Caroline gave a slow nod.
"Most likely."
Max looked toward the path beyond the entrance, then back at the eye attached to him.
His voice turned calm again, though the coldness in it made everyone still their breath.
"Fine," he said.
"If it is a curse, then we will deal with it later."
He then looked at Caroline.
"But first, we leave this place."
The others nodded, though the unease in their eyes remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 1773: Lunarian Kingdom!
paragraphs: "Let us go," Max said as he began to move despite the little eye still stuck to his left shoulder.
The small cursed eye blinked slowly as it shifted against him, and every now and then, its tiny red-black pupil moved as if studying the surroundings.

Sometimes it stayed on his shoulder. Sometimes it slid slightly across his upper arm. Sometimes it floated just a hair’s breadth away from his body before attaching itself again, as if it was neither fully physical nor fully illusory.

The sight was disturbing to everyone else, but Max did not pay it much attention after realizing that brute force could not destroy it for now. As long as this thing did not restrict his movement or interfere in his battles, he could not care less about it at the moment.
With that, the group once again began moving.
Max walked at the front, Dragonheart resting in his hand, while Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the other third faction elves followed closely behind him.

The path out of Witch God Valley was still filled with cursed mist, but after the death of the Abyssal Witch Eye, the pressure near the entrance had clearly weakened. The strange whispers in the air were still there, the black grass still moved without wind, and the twisted trees still seemed to watch them from both sides, but nothing dared to stop them openly.

Perhaps the death of the guardian had shaken the valley. Perhaps the little eye attached to Max had marked him in a way that made the other cursed things hesitate. Whatever the reason, their path became strangely smooth.
In no time, they arrived near the edge of the Witch God Tree.

The vast treetop world spread behind them like a cursed kingdom above the clouds, while ahead of them was the massive trunk descending into the lower sky. Countless enormous branches extended outward like mountain ridges, and thick clouds rolled beneath them, hiding the lower parts of the tree from sight.

From this height, the world below looked distant and unreal, and the enormous scale of the Witch God Tree became even more shocking. Its trunk fell through the clouds like a pillar holding up the heavens, while glowing veins within its bark pulsed faintly, as though the whole ancient tree was alive and watching their departure.
Max stopped at the edge and looked downward.

His Dimensional Sovereign Body spread its senses along the space below, but because the Witch God Tree was too large and covered in too many cursed distortions, he could not clearly see everything waiting near the bottom.
Still, the feeling in his heart told him that the path ahead would not be peaceful. Seraphine, Fin, Lumine, and the others had all been killed, but they still had lives left.

Once they revived outside, the second faction would quickly understand that Caroline had been rescued and that Max was involved. If those people were not stupid, then they would not let them leave so easily.
Max turned back and looked at everyone.
"Stay cautious," he said calmly.
Caroline’s expression became serious. "You think the second faction has people waiting below?"

"I do," Max said. "They already sent Seraphine, Fin, Lumine, and others to hunt you. Since those people failed, they will either prepare an ambush or gather more people near the bottom of the Witch God Tree. Once we reach below, there is a good chance they will attack us immediately."
Jessica clenched her sword. "Then we should descend carefully."

Max nodded. "Do not scatter. If the second faction attacks, stay behind me unless I tell you otherwise. Their target will likely be Caroline first, but after what happened inside the valley, they will also come for me."
One of the injured third faction elves said with hesitation, "Lord Max, if they have too many people..."
Max looked at him.
The elf immediately stopped speaking.
Max’s expression remained calm, but his eyes carried a cold certainty. "Numbers only matter when they can hurt me."
No one spoke after that.

Caroline looked at Max’s back, and although she wanted to remind him not to underestimate the second faction, the words did not come out. She had seen him kill Seraphine and Fin. She had seen him cut down the guardian of Witch God Valley. She had seen the power of his Divine Veins, Draconic Essences, sword path, and bloodline.
At this point, warning him like he was an ordinary young genius felt meaningless. Max understood danger, but he did not fear it. That was the difference.
Nancy moved closer to him and said quietly, "If Princess Rosaline intercepted the news, she may also come here."
Max glanced at her. "Will she be an enemy?"

Nancy hesitated for a moment. "I do not know. She is a princess of the Lunarian Kingdom ruling a good chunk of many star realms and her force is also considered one of the strongest 1st rate forces standing on equal terms with Sword God Palace and War God Palace."
She added. "Since you have killed his men before coming here, there might be a chance she would intercept you."
Max looked down at the clouds below. "Then she can speak after I deal with the ones trying to stop us."
The little cursed eye on his shoulder blinked once, its red-black pupil rolling slightly as if it had heard him.
Max ignored it.
"Let us descend."

The moment he said that, he stepped off the edge of the treetop and began flying downward along the massive trunk of the Witch God Tree. Golden light flickered faintly around his body, not enough to reveal his full bloodline power, but enough to cut through the cursed wind rushing upward from below.
Nancy followed closely behind him, while Caroline, Jessica, and the remaining third faction elves moved in formation, keeping themselves within the range Max had indicated.
The descent began.
The clouds swallowed them almost immediately.

Cold mist rushed past their bodies, and the enormous bark of the Witch God Tree blurred beside them as they flew downward. Strange creatures hidden in the holes of the trunk watched them pass, but none dared to attack.

Some roots twitched from the bark as if tempted to lash out, but the moment Max’s gaze swept over them, they withdrew silently. The group continued falling through layer after layer of clouds, moving from the cursed upper world toward the lower regions of the Eternal Hourglass.

chapters.title: Chapter 1774: Surrounded - 1
paragraphs: In no time, Max and the others arrived at the base of the Witch God Tree.
However, just when they reached the base, a golden sword flashed toward them out of nowhere.

The sword was not held by anyone. It appeared from the air itself, formed from condensed golden light, and it moved so quickly that several of the injured third faction elves did not even realize they were being attacked until the light had already crossed half the distance. Its target was not Max.

It was Caroline. The blade carried a sharp bloodline-suppressing force, and the moment it appeared, Caroline’s Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline trembled faintly, clearly reacting to the power hidden within the attack.
Max immediately moved forward and slashed Dragonheart at the incoming golden sword.
Boom!

The golden sword shattered into countless fragments of light, and the impact spread across the base of the Witch God Tree like a golden storm. The surrounding dust and dead leaves were swept away, the huge roots beneath their feet trembled, and several nearby stone ridges were sliced open by the stray sword light.
Max stood in front of everyone with Dragonheart lowered slightly in his hand, but his eyes had already become cold because the scene before them was much worse than they had imagined.
They were surrounded.

All around the base of the Witch God Tree, dozens upon dozens of elves stood in formation, each one wearing armor marked with the symbol of the second faction. Some stood on the giant roots spreading across the ground, some floated in the air with wings of light behind them, and some stood silently in the gaps between the ancient stones surrounding the tree’s base.

Their auras were far stronger than the ordinary hunters Max had encountered before, and unlike Lumine’s group, these elves had clearly come prepared. Light formations were already active beneath their feet, golden chains hovered in the air around the battlefield, and several bloodline-suppressing talismans had been placed around the base of the tree, forming a wide sealed region that trapped Max’s group inside.
Seraphine and Fin stood among them.

Both of them had revived after being killed in Witch God Valley, but their faces were no longer arrogant like before. Seraphine’s expression was icy, yet there was still a trace of fear hidden deep in her eyes when she looked at Max.

Fin’s usual mocking smile had disappeared completely, and although he still held his sword, his grip was tighter than before, as if his hand remembered the feeling of being cut down by Max’s Emotion Severing Path.
Their hatred was obvious, but so was their caution. They had already learned that Max was not someone they could handle alone.
At the center of the second faction formation stood a golden-haired elf woman.
The moment Caroline saw her, her face changed.
"Max," Caroline said in a low and tense voice, "be careful. The elf woman with golden hair standing at the center is Selene Vaeloria, the Divine Daughter of the second faction."
Max’s eyes shifted toward the golden-haired elf woman.
Selene Vaeloria truly looked different from the others.

Her golden hair flowed down her back like liquid sunlight, and her eyes were a clear, sacred gold that carried both nobility and coldness. She wore a white-gold battle dress covered in delicate divine patterns, and behind her floated a faint halo of Heavenly Luminance power.

Compared to Seraphine’s bloodline aura, Selene’s was far purer and more oppressive. The light around her did not simply shine. It seemed to command the surrounding radiance to kneel, and every second faction elf around her looked at her with unmistakable reverence.
She looked at Max calmly.
"So you are Max Morgan," Selene said, her voice soft but filled with authority. "The human who killed Seraphine, Fin, Lumine, and many others of my faction."
Max did not answer immediately.

The small cursed eye on his left shoulder blinked once, slowly turning its pupil toward Selene, while Dragonheart gave out a faint hum in his hand. Max noticed Selene’s Heavenly Luminance aura and felt something strange inside his bloodline stir faintly, but the reaction was not one of kinship. It was closer to disgust, as if his bloodline itself rejected the presence of the second faction’s divine radiance.

Caroline stepped closer to Max and whispered, "She is dangerous. Seraphine and Fin are powerful, but Selene is one of the true cores of the second faction’s younger generation. She was trained directly by the Bloodline Hall and the ancestors."
Jessica’s face was pale as she looked at Selene. "I did not think they would send the Divine Daughter herself."

Selene’s gaze moved from Max to Caroline, and a faint smile appeared on her lips. "Caroline, you truly are troublesome. Even after hiding inside Witch God Valley, you still managed to come out alive. I suppose I should thank this human for bringing you out instead of forcing us to enter that cursed place again."
Caroline’s eyes turned cold. "You should have stayed away."
Selene smiled lightly. "And allow you to escape? No. The remnants of Caelira’s faction belong in the Elf Prison, and you, more than anyone else, should return there."
The words made the third faction elves behind Caroline tremble with anger.
Max’s gaze became colder, but before he could speak, Nancy suddenly looked toward the other side of the battlefield.
"There are others here," she said quietly.
Max turned slightly.
On the opposite side of the base, away from the second faction formation, another group of people stood gathered beneath the shadow of the Witch God Tree. They were not part of the second faction.

Their armor and robes were different, more refined, and bore the emblem of the Lunarian Kingdom, one of the strongest first-rate forces in the Divine Realm. At their front stood Princess Rosaline, her white and rose-gold gown moving gently in the wind, her golden-pink hair shining faintly beneath the dim light of the Eternal Hourglass.
The young man who had stopped the Sword God Palace disciples earlier stood beside her, along with several powerful Lunarian experts and other followers.

chapters.title: Chapter 1775: Surrounded - 2
paragraphs: Princess Rosaline’s gaze was fixed on Max.

She did not look surprised to see him. It was clear that she had already expected him to come out from the Witch God Tree. Her expression was thoughtful, and when her eyes moved briefly to the small cursed eye attached to his shoulder, a strange light flashed across her face.
Then her gaze shifted to Selene and the second faction elves, and her expression became slightly colder.
"So the Lunarian Kingdom is here too," Caroline said, her voice heavy.
Jessica clenched her sword. "Princess Rosaline."
Max glanced at Nancy. "Is that her?"
Nancy nodded. "Yes. Princess Rosaline of the Lunarian Kingdom."
For a moment, the base of the Witch God Tree became silent in a suffocating way.
Max’s group stood in the middle.
On one side was Selene Vaeloria, the Divine Daughter of the second faction, accompanied by Seraphine, Fin, and a large number of second faction elites.
On the other side was Princess Rosaline of the Lunarian Kingdom, watching the situation with her own group.

The cursed trunk of the Witch God Tree towered behind them like a dark pillar vanishing into the clouds, while the huge roots beneath their feet formed a natural battlefield. The air was tense enough to feel like it might crack at any moment. Everyone knew that the smallest movement could turn this place into a battlefield between multiple forces.
Selene looked toward Rosaline and smiled faintly. "Princess Rosaline, are you here to interfere?"
Rosaline’s expression remained calm. "I am here to observe."

Seraphine sneered. "Observe? This human killed members of the second faction and helped fugitives of the Elf Prison escape. There is nothing to observe. He should be captured, and Caroline should be returned to where she belongs."
Rosaline’s eyes narrowed slightly. "The Lunarian Kingdom doesn’t care what your elf faction does or doesn’t."
The second faction elves immediately stirred.
Selene raised one hand, and they went silent.
Then she looked at Max again.
"You are right." Selene said with a smile. "You don’t care and let it be like this."
She then turned to Max. "What about you human boy?"
Max looked at her calmly. "You will either run away like a coward or die by my sword. That is the only outcome I can see here."
"Your arrogance knows no bounds." Selene sneered hearing Max. "To make me run away? You sure dream a lot."

"Dream?" Max also sneered as his Dragonheart trembled a little in his hands. "Oh, believe me when I say out of all the opponents I have killed, you will be one of the few I would enjoy killing the most."
Selene’s eyes moved to Dragonheart, then to the little cursed eye on his shoulder, and finally back to his face.
"You carry many interesting things," she said. "The Sword of the Sword Sovereign, a strange curse mark from Witch God Valley, and perhaps... something else."
The last words carried a deeper meaning.
Max understood what she was hinting at.
Caroline’s face turned tense. She knew that if Selene sensed Max’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, the situation could become even worse.
Max, however, did not look nervous at all.
He simply stepped forward.
The moment he moved, Seraphine and Fin both stiffened instinctively, and several second faction elves raised their weapons at once.
Max’s gaze swept across them, then stopped on Selene.
"You brought a lot of people," he said calmly.
Selene smiled. "Enough to stop you."
Max’s smile became colder.
"Are you sure?"
Selene sneered.

Just as she was about to release her power, her eyes suddenly shifted toward a certain direction, and the golden halo behind her trembled faintly as if it had sensed something approaching from the shadows.

Almost at the same time, Max also turned his head in that direction. His Dimensional Sovereign Body had already felt them long before they chose to reveal themselves. Three auras were hiding at the edge of the battlefield, but their attempt at concealment was almost laughable in Max’s eyes, because each of them carried a presence so strong and distinct that they appeared in his perception like three blazing suns standing in the dark.
"Just reveal yourselves," Max said calmly, his voice spreading across the base of the Witch God Tree. "The auras of you three are bright as suns in the dark. There is no use hiding."
The moment Max’s words fell, the air in that direction rippled.
A soft laugh sounded first.

It was gentle, elegant, and strangely eerie, as if a beautiful woman was laughing from inside an ancient dream. The cursed mist beside one of the huge roots of the Witch God Tree twisted into a spiral, and from that spiral, a young woman slowly stepped out.

She wore a long black-violet dress decorated with silver star patterns, and a pointed witch hat sat above her long midnight-blue hair. Her eyes were deep purple, filled with starlight, and several small crystal charms floated around her like tiny moons.

The moment she appeared, the cursed aura around the Witch God Tree reacted to her presence, but instead of attacking, it seemed to hesitate, as if recognizing another wielder of strange and ancient powers.
Caroline’s expression changed slightly. "A witch..."
Nancy’s eyes sharpened. "Stellar Templar."
The woman smiled faintly and gave a graceful bow that looked playful rather than respectful. "How sharp. I thought I had hidden myself quite well, but it seems I was wrong."
Her voice carried a soft charm, yet no one present dared to treat her lightly.

Stellar Templar was one of the seven strongest first-rate forces of the Divine Realm. Unlike ordinary sects, clans, kingdoms, or courts, Stellar Templar was famous for producing witches, star-seers, curse masters, fate readers, and mystic spellcasters whose methods were often difficult to understand and even harder to defend against.

Among the seven first-rate forces, they were not known for direct brute strength, but no one wanted to offend them easily, because a witch from Stellar Templar could curse an enemy, manipulate the battlefield, read hidden dangers, or guide fate itself in terrifying ways.
Selene’s eyes narrowed. "Morgana Starveil."
The witch smiled. "It seems Divine Daughter Selene still remembers me."
Morgana Starveil.
One of the strongest geniuses of Stellar Templar.

The moment that name spread, several elves from the second faction showed wary expressions, while even Princess Rosaline’s calm gaze became more serious. Morgana was not a weak spectator who had come to watch from the side. In this Cosmic Ascension Conference, she was one of the people truly qualified to stand on the highest stage among the younger generation.

sentences.text: Princess Rosaline’s gaze was fixed on Max.
She did not look surprised to see him.
It was clear that she had already expected him to come out from the Witch God Tree.
Her expression was thoughtful, and when her eyes moved briefly to the small cursed eye attached to his shoulder, a strange light flashed across her face.
Then her gaze shifted to Selene and the second faction elves, and her expression became slightly colder.
"So the Lunarian Kingdom is here too," Caroline said, her voice heavy.
Jessica clenched her sword.
"Princess Rosaline."
Max glanced at Nancy.
"Is that her?"
Nancy nodded.
"Yes.
Princess Rosaline of the Lunarian Kingdom."
For a moment, the base of the Witch God Tree became silent in a suffocating way.
Max’s group stood in the middle.
On one side was Selene Vaeloria, the Divine Daughter of the second faction, accompanied by Seraphine, Fin, and a large number of second faction elites.
On the other side was Princess Rosaline of the Lunarian Kingdom, watching the situation with her own group.
The cursed trunk of the Witch God Tree towered behind them like a dark pillar vanishing into the clouds, while the huge roots beneath their feet formed a natural battlefield.
The air was tense enough to feel like it might crack at any moment.
Everyone knew that the smallest movement could turn this place into a battlefield between multiple forces.
Selene looked toward Rosaline and smiled faintly.
"Princess Rosaline, are you here to interfere?"
Rosaline’s expression remained calm.
"I am here to observe."
Seraphine sneered.
"Observe?
This human killed members of the second faction and helped fugitives of the Elf Prison escape.
There is nothing to observe.
He should be captured, and Caroline should be returned to where she belongs."
Rosaline’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"The Lunarian Kingdom doesn’t care what your elf faction does or doesn’t."
The second faction elves immediately stirred.
Selene raised one hand, and they went silent.
Then she looked at Max again.
"You are right." Selene said with a smile.
"You don’t care and let it be like this."
She then turned to Max.
"What about you human boy?"
Max looked at her calmly.
"You will either run away like a coward or die by my sword.
That is the only outcome I can see here."
"Your arrogance knows no bounds." Selene sneered hearing Max.
"To make me run away?
You sure dream a lot."
"Dream?" Max also sneered as his Dragonheart trembled a little in his hands.
"Oh, believe me when I say out of all the opponents I have killed, you will be one of the few I would enjoy killing the most."
Selene’s eyes moved to Dragonheart, then to the little cursed eye on his shoulder, and finally back to his face.
"You carry many interesting things," she said.
"The Sword of the Sword Sovereign, a strange curse mark from Witch God Valley, and perhaps... something else."
The last words carried a deeper meaning.
Max understood what she was hinting at.
Caroline’s face turned tense.
She knew that if Selene sensed Max’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, the situation could become even worse.
Max, however, did not look nervous at all.
He simply stepped forward.
The moment he moved, Seraphine and Fin both stiffened instinctively, and several second faction elves raised their weapons at once.
Max’s gaze swept across them, then stopped on Selene.
"You brought a lot of people," he said calmly.
Selene smiled.
"Enough to stop you."
Max’s smile became colder.
"Are you sure?"
Selene sneered.

Just as she was about to release her power, her eyes suddenly shifted toward a certain direction, and the golden halo behind her trembled faintly as if it had sensed something approaching from the shadows.
Almost at the same time, Max also turned his head in that direction.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body had already felt them long before they chose to reveal themselves.

Three auras were hiding at the edge of the battlefield, but their attempt at concealment was almost laughable in Max’s eyes, because each of them carried a presence so strong and distinct that they appeared in his perception like three blazing suns standing in the dark.
"Just reveal yourselves," Max said calmly, his voice spreading across the base of the Witch God Tree.
"The auras of you three are bright as suns in the dark.
There is no use hiding."
The moment Max’s words fell, the air in that direction rippled.
A soft laugh sounded first.
It was gentle, elegant, and strangely eerie, as if a beautiful woman was laughing from inside an ancient dream.
The cursed mist beside one of the huge roots of the Witch God Tree twisted into a spiral, and from that spiral, a young woman slowly stepped out.
She wore a long black-violet dress decorated with silver star patterns, and a pointed witch hat sat above her long midnight-blue hair.
Her eyes were deep purple, filled with starlight, and several small crystal charms floated around her like tiny moons.

The moment she appeared, the cursed aura around the Witch God Tree reacted to her presence, but instead of attacking, it seemed to hesitate, as if recognizing another wielder of strange and ancient powers.
Caroline’s expression changed slightly.
"A witch..."
Nancy’s eyes sharpened.
"Stellar Templar."
The woman smiled faintly and gave a graceful bow that looked playful rather than respectful.
"How sharp.
I thought I had hidden myself quite well, but it seems I was wrong."
Her voice carried a soft charm, yet no one present dared to treat her lightly.
Stellar Templar was one of the seven strongest first-rate forces of the Divine Realm.

Unlike ordinary sects, clans, kingdoms, or courts, Stellar Templar was famous for producing witches, star-seers, curse masters, fate readers, and mystic spellcasters whose methods were often difficult to understand and even harder to defend against.

Among the seven first-rate forces, they were not known for direct brute strength, but no one wanted to offend them easily, because a witch from Stellar Templar could curse an enemy, manipulate the battlefield, read hidden dangers, or guide fate itself in terrifying ways.
Selene’s eyes narrowed.
"Morgana Starveil."
The witch smiled.
"It seems Divine Daughter Selene still remembers me."
Morgana Starveil.
One of the strongest geniuses of Stellar Templar.
The moment that name spread, several elves from the second faction showed wary expressions, while even Princess Rosaline’s calm gaze became more serious.
Morgana was not a weak spectator who had come to watch from the side.
In this Cosmic Ascension Conference, she was one of the people truly qualified to stand on the highest stage among the younger generation.

chapters.title: Chapter 1776: Surrounded - 3
paragraphs: Before anyone could speak further, another aura appeared.
The space beside Morgana folded inward silently.

There was no explosion, no light, and no grand entrance, yet the moment the space folded, everyone felt as if the distance between them and that direction had become meaningless. A young man stepped out from the folded space, dressed in a simple white robe with black edges.

His long hair was tied loosely behind him, his eyes were silver-gray, and his expression was calm to the point of indifference. Around him, faint traces of void power moved like transparent water, causing the air near his body to distort and rebuild itself again and again.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
This person’s aura was different from the others. And most importantly, he could sense the aura of Void Genesis Art from this man.
Rosaline slowly said, "Kaiden Voidmere of the Grand Void Sanctum."
The young man glanced at her calmly but did not respond.

The Grand Void Sanctum was another one of the seven strongest first-rate forces of the Divine Realm, and its disciples were famous for their mastery over space, void laws, and strange movement techniques that made them almost impossible to trap. Among them, Kaiden Voidmere was known as the strongest genius of his generation.

Some said he had been born inside a collapsing void rift and survived because the void itself acknowledged him. Others said he had already touched the edge of a Pseudo Cosmic Path related to emptiness and distance, making him one of the most dangerous participants in the entire Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Kaiden’s gaze moved to Max.
For a brief moment, his calm eyes flickered.
The two stared at each other for a moment.
No killing intent appeared between them, but the air around them became tense in a different way, as if two people who understood the same type of danger had recognized each other instantly.
Then the third aura descended.

Unlike Morgana’s eerie mystic presence or Kaiden’s silent void pressure, this aura was direct, grand, and overbearing. Nine points of starlight appeared in the sky above the base of the Witch God Tree, and each star shone with a different shade of silver, gold, blue, red, white, purple, black, green, and crimson.
The nine stars revolved once, then descended together, forming a stairway of starlight. From that stairway, a young man walked down step by step.

He wore dark-gold battle armor engraved with nine star marks, and his black hair moved wildly in the wind. His eyes were bright like burning stars, and every step he took caused the ground beneath the Witch God Tree to tremble faintly.

Compared to Morgana and Kaiden, he made no attempt to hide his strength. His aura was bold, sharp, and filled with absolute confidence, as if he believed that every battlefield he entered should naturally make room for him.
Caroline’s face became even more solemn. "Nine Star Court."
Jessica swallowed. "The strongest first-rate force..."

Nine Star Court was often called the strongest first-rate force in the Divine Realm. Even among the seven strongest first-rate forces, its reputation stood at the top. Its disciples cultivated star power, body power, combat arts, and star formations, and their inheritance was famous for producing monsters who could fight across levels with terrifying ease.

Many people believed that if Nine Star Court ever produced a true supreme genius capable of uniting its nine great star inheritances, that person might one day challenge even the weakest supreme forces.
Selene’s expression finally lost some of its ease. "Orion Starfall."
The young man in dark-gold armor smiled broadly. "Selene, you look unhappy to see me."
Orion Starfall.
The strongest genius of Nine Star Court.

His name alone caused the battlefield to become even heavier. Even Seraphine and Fin, who had been arrogant before Max crushed them, looked deeply cautious now. They might look down on many people, but they would never dare to look down on Orion Starfall.

Among the younger generation of the seven strongest first-rate forces, his reputation was terrifying, and there were already rumors that he had defeated several peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses without using his full strength.

With Morgana Starveil of Stellar Templar, Kaiden Voidmere of the Grand Void Sanctum, and Orion Starfall of Nine Star Court appearing at the same time, the situation at the base of the Witch God Tree instantly became far more complicated.
Max’s group stood in the center.
Selene and the second faction elves stood on one side.
Princess Rosaline and the Lunarian Kingdom stood on another.
And now, three more monsters from three of the seven strongest first-rate forces had appeared.
The base of the Witch God Tree no longer looked like a simple ambush.
It looked like the gathering point of the strongest young geniuses of the Divine Realm.

Morgana’s purple eyes moved to the small cursed eye attached to Max’s shoulder, and a trace of curiosity appeared on her face. "A Witch’s curse mark. How interesting. I felt the death of the Abyssal Witch Eye and came to see who had the courage to kill the old guardian, but I did not expect the person to be carrying the mark so calmly."
Kaiden looked at Max’s shoulder as well, then at Dragonheart. "He also carries the Sword of the Sword Sovereign."
Orion laughed. "And he is the same Max Morgan whose ranking jumped like a madman. Good. I was wondering when I would meet him."
Selene’s face became colder.

She had intended to deal with Max and Caroline quickly, but the arrival of Morgana, Kaiden, and Orion changed the balance completely. None of these three belonged to weak powers, and none of them would obey her. Even worse, each of them had clearly come because of Max, the Witch’s curse mark, the Sword of the Sword Sovereign, or the commotion around Witch God Valley.
Max looked at the three newcomers calmly.
"You three came to fight too?"
Morgana smiled. "Not necessarily. I sensed that someone destroyed the guardian here and came to check."
Kaiden replied flatly, "That depends."
Orion grinned. "I came to see if you are as strong as the rumors say."
Max’s expression did not change.

The little cursed eye on his shoulder blinked again, slowly turning from Selene to Morgana, then to Kaiden, then to Orion, as if even the curse itself was watching the arrival of these powerful geniuses with interest.
Rosaline looked at the scene and sighed softly. "Now this has truly become troublesome."
Selene’s golden eyes moved between Max and the three newcomers, then her lips curled into a cold smile again.
"Interesting," she said. "It seems everyone wants a piece of you, Max Morgan."
Max held Dragonheart loosely at his side.
His gaze swept across Selene, Seraphine, Fin, Rosaline, Morgana, Kaiden, and Orion.
Then he smiled faintly.
"If all of you are done introducing yourselves," Max said calmly, "decide quickly whether you are here to watch or to stand in my way."

chapters.title: Chapter 1777: Max vs Selene
paragraphs: Selene sneered at Max’s words before turning to Rosaline.
"Remember your words."
"Do as you please," Princess Rosaline said calmly.

She had only been interested in Max because of the terrifying sword aura he had left behind near the neutral city, and after seeing the situation at the base of the Witch God Tree, that interest had only grown deeper.

The Sword of the Sword Sovereign, the strange Witch’s curse mark clinging to his body, the rumors of his sudden rise in the Cosmic Ascension Ranking List, and now the way Seraphine and Fin looked at him with fear hidden beneath hatred all made Rosaline feel that Max was far more mysterious than the reports suggested.
If letting Selene fight him would force him to release that terrifying sword aura again, then so be it. For now, Rosaline was willing to remain an observer.
Selene understood Rosaline’s meaning, and her cold smile deepened slightly before she turned back toward Max.
Then she raised one hand.
"All of you, step back."

The second faction elves immediately reacted. Some looked startled, while others hesitated because they had clearly come here prepared to surround Max and Caroline together, but none of them dared to disobey Selene’s command.
Seraphine and Fin exchanged a brief glance, and although resentment filled their eyes, their bodies moved backward more quickly than the others. They had already fought Max once.
They knew better than anyone that if Selene truly wanted to take him on herself, standing too close to the battlefield would only place them inside the range of that emotionless sword path again.
One of the second faction elves said carefully, "Divine Daughter, should we not assist you? This human is not simple."
Selene’s golden eyes turned toward him.
The elf immediately lowered his head and retreated without another word.
"I said step back," Selene said lightly. "I will take care of him with my own hands."

Her voice was soft, but the authority inside it could not be questioned. The second faction formation slowly opened, and the elves moved away from the central battlefield, creating a wide circular space at the base of the Witch God Tree.

The golden talismans and bloodline-suppressing formations around the area remained active, but the people controlling them withdrew to the edges, leaving Selene standing alone in front of Max. Her long golden hair moved gently behind her, the halo of Heavenly Luminance power above her shoulders becoming brighter with each passing second.
The atmosphere shifted.
This was no longer an ambush.
It was a duel.
Morgana Starveil watched with bright purple eyes, her smile playful but focused. "The Divine Daughter wants to fight him herself. How bold."
Kaiden Voidmere remained silent, but the space around him rippled faintly, showing that even he was paying close attention.
Orion Starfall crossed his arms and laughed. "Good. This is better than watching a bunch of people rush him together."
Rosaline did not speak. Her gaze remained fixed on Max.
Max, however, only looked at Selene for a moment before turning toward Caroline and the others.
"Retreat."
Caroline frowned. "Max..."
"I will handle everything here," Max said calmly.
His tone did not leave room for argument.

Caroline wanted to say more, but when she saw the calm certainty in his eyes, she swallowed her words. She still knew too little about Max, but after everything she had witnessed inside Witch God Valley, she understood one thing clearly.
Her sister’s son was not reckless without reason. If he told them to retreat, it meant he had already decided how to face what came next.
Jessica immediately helped Caroline move back, while the other third faction elves followed with tense expressions. Nancy also retreated, though her eyes remained on Max the entire time.
Caroline stopped several dozen meters away and looked back at Max.
"Be careful," she said quietly.
Max did not look back, but he nodded once.

The little cursed eye on his left shoulder blinked slowly, shifting across his shoulder as if it was also watching Selene. Max ignored it. His right hand held Dragonheart loosely at his side, and his expression remained calm, almost indifferent, while Selene’s aura continued rising in front of him.
Selene looked at him with cold interest.
"You are quite confident," she said. "You stand here alone even though you know who I am."
Max looked at her. "I know enough."
Selene smiled. "Then you should also know that I am not Seraphine, Fin, or Lumine."
"I know," Max replied.
His gaze moved briefly to the golden halo behind her.
"You are more useful than them."
Selene’s eyes narrowed slightly.

The words sounded simple, but she understood the meaning. Max was not treating her as a greater danger. He was treating her as someone who might carry more answers, more Killing Points, and more connection to the truth about his stolen bloodline.
The smile on Selene’s face slowly faded.
"You truly do not know how to lower your head."
Max’s expression remained unchanged. "I do not lower my head to thieves."
The air instantly froze.
The second faction elves at the edge of the battlefield stirred, and several of them released sharp killing intent, but Selene raised one finger without looking back, stopping them again.
Rosaline’s eyes sharpened slightly.
Morgana’s smile widened.
Kaiden’s gaze became deeper.
Orion’s expression turned more excited.

Caroline’s heart clenched because she knew exactly what Max was referring to. The bloodline stolen from him as a child. The second faction’s forbidden extraction. The Divine Son who now carried what should have belonged to Max.
By calling Selene and her faction thieves in front of everyone, Max had not merely insulted her. He had pointed directly at one of the darkest secrets of the second faction.
Selene’s golden light became colder.
"Careful, Max Morgan," she said softly. "Some words carry consequences."
Max slowly raised Dragonheart.
"I am counting on it."
A faint sword hum spread across the battlefield.
Selene’s halo brightened.
The ground beneath them trembled.

Around the battlefield, everyone had already stepped back. Rosaline, Morgana, Kaiden, Orion, Seraphine, Fin, the second faction elves, Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the third faction remnants all watched the two figures standing beneath the vast shadow of the Witch God Tree.
On one side stood Selene Vaeloria, the Divine Daughter of the second faction, trained by the Bloodline Hall and the ancestors, carrying an extremely pure Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline.

On the other side stood Max Morgan, Caelira’s son, wielder of Dragonheart, bearer of the Witch’s curse mark, owner of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, and the one who had already cut down every enemy who believed numbers, status, or reputation could stop him.
Selene took one step forward, and golden light poured from her body like a rising sun.
Max’s eyes remained calm as Dragonheart tilted slightly in his hand.
The duel was about to begin.
