The smile on Selene’s face slowly faded.
"You truly do not know how to lower your head."
Max’s expression remained unchanged.
"I do not lower my head to thieves."
The air instantly froze.
The second faction elves at the edge of the battlefield stirred, and several of them released sharp killing intent, but Selene raised one finger without looking back, stopping them again.
Rosaline’s eyes sharpened slightly.
Morgana’s smile widened.
Kaiden’s gaze became deeper.
Orion’s expression turned more excited.
Caroline’s heart clenched because she knew exactly what Max was referring to.
The bloodline stolen from him as a child.
The second faction’s forbidden extraction.
The Divine Son who now carried what should have belonged to Max.
By calling Selene and her faction thieves in front of everyone, Max had not merely insulted her.
He had pointed directly at one of the darkest secrets of the second faction.
Selene’s golden light became colder.
"Careful, Max Morgan," she said softly.
"Some words carry consequences."
Max slowly raised Dragonheart.
"I am counting on it."
A faint sword hum spread across the battlefield.
Selene’s halo brightened.
The ground beneath them trembled.
Around the battlefield, everyone had already stepped back.

Rosaline, Morgana, Kaiden, Orion, Seraphine, Fin, the second faction elves, Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the third faction remnants all watched the two figures standing beneath the vast shadow of the Witch God Tree.
On one side stood Selene Vaeloria, the Divine Daughter of the second faction, trained by the Bloodline Hall and the ancestors, carrying an extremely pure Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline.

On the other side stood Max Morgan, Caelira’s son, wielder of Dragonheart, bearer of the Witch’s curse mark, owner of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, and the one who had already cut down every enemy who believed numbers, status, or reputation could stop him.
Selene took one step forward, and golden light poured from her body like a rising sun.
Max’s eyes remained calm as Dragonheart tilted slightly in his hand.
The duel was about to begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 1778: Divine King’s Punishment!
paragraphs: Max did not intend to hold back in this battle.

If Selene had been someone from another force, perhaps he might have tested her slowly, measured her strength, and used the fight to sharpen one of his paths. But she was not simply another genius standing in his way.

She was the Divine Daughter of the second faction, a core figure raised by the same people who had destroyed his family, stolen his bloodline, imprisoned his parents, tortured the members of his mother’s faction, and hunted Caroline all the way into Witch God Valley.
Against an elf of the second faction, especially one standing so close to the center of its younger generation, Max saw no reason to be patient.
The air around him changed before Selene could make the first move.

Dragonheart remained in his hand, but the power rising from Max this time was not the deathly stillness of the Emotion Severing Path. It was not the ancient pressure of his Draconic Essences, nor was it the sacred golden radiance of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.

A different force erupted from him, violent, majestic, destructive, and filled with the authority of punishment. Seven colors of lightning appeared around his body, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet, each strand moving like a living divine serpent as they coiled through the air and gathered behind him into a vast lightning domain.
The sky above the base of the Witch God Tree darkened.
Thunder roared.

The huge roots beneath Max’s feet trembled as the seven-colored lightning spread outward, and even the golden light released by Selene seemed to pause for a brief moment beneath the pressure of that punishment aura.

This was Max’s Pseudo Cosmic Path of seven-colored lightning, a path he had created after considering two foundations. The first was the essence of the Storm King’s Inheritance, which had taught him the majesty of storms, thunder, heavenly pressure, and the way lightning could dominate a battlefield.
The second was the destructive and punishment nature of the seven-colored lightning itself, a force that did not merely strike, but judged, destroyed, and erased those standing beneath its wrath.
"Divine King Punishment," Max said calmly.
The moment the name fell, the seven-colored lightning behind him exploded into the shape of a towering divine throne made of thunderclouds and punishment light.

No figure sat upon the throne, but everyone present felt the terrifying illusion of an unseen king looking down at all things from above. Lightning laws, punishment intent, and storm authority gathered around Max, making him look as if he had become the executor of a divine sentence.
Selene’s expression changed slightly.

She had expected Max to use his sword path, especially after hearing from Seraphine and Fin about the terrifying emotionless Pseudo Cosmic Path that had crushed them inside Witch God Valley. She had even prepared herself for his sword aura.
But instead of that, Max had released another Pseudo Cosmic Path, and this one was completely different. It was not silent. It was not cold. It was violent, majestic, and oppressively destructive.
Rosaline’s eyes narrowed from the distance. "Another Pseudo Cosmic Path?"
Morgana Starveil’s smile slowly faded into genuine interest. "Seven-colored lightning with the authority of punishment. How interesting. This is not a simple lightning path."
Kaiden Voidmere stared at the space around Max and said nothing, but the slight ripple around his body showed that he was no longer as indifferent as before.
Orion Starfall laughed loudly, his eyes burning with fighting intent. "Good! This Max Morgan is even better than the rumors."

Selene quickly suppressed the surprise in her heart. As the Divine Daughter of the second faction, she would never allow herself to show fear before so many powerful geniuses. Golden light burst from her body, and the halo behind her expanded into a radiant circle several dozen meters wide.

Unlike Seraphine’s Radiant Judgment Path, Selene’s power was purer and more regal. It did not create a divine court to judge enemies. Instead, it turned the battlefield itself into a sacred domain of light.
"Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline, Divine Radiant Crown."

A crown of golden light appeared above Selene’s head, and the moment it formed, her aura rose sharply. Countless beams of light descended around her like pillars holding up a sacred palace, and every beam carried a suppressive power that targeted bloodlines, spiritual energy, and concepts at the same time.
She lifted one hand, and hundreds of golden swords formed behind her, each one brighter and sharper than the sword that had attacked Caroline earlier.
"Luminance Sword Rain."
The golden swords shot forward.

They did not fly chaotically. They moved with perfect order, forming intersecting paths that sealed Max’s front, sides, and sky above him. Every sword contained compressed light, and as they descended, the air was burned clean, the mist was erased, and the ground beneath the Witch God Tree began glowing as if forced to reflect Selene’s radiance.
Max raised his hand.
Seven-colored lightning gathered around his fingers.
He did not swing Dragonheart.
He simply pointed forward.
A storm of lightning erupted.
Boom!

The seven-colored thunderbolts collided with the golden sword rain in midair. The first moment of impact lit up the entire battlefield, and golden light clashed with seven-colored lightning so violently that many weaker elves had to cover their eyes.

Selene’s light swords were powerful, refined, and filled with bloodline suppression, but the moment they touched Max’s Divine King Punishment, they began cracking under the destructive punishment force contained inside the lightning.
One golden sword shattered.
Then ten.
Then hundreds.
The seven-colored lightning tore through the sword rain like heavenly punishment falling upon a false sun, reducing every radiant blade into golden sparks that scattered through the air.

Selene’s eyes sharpened, and with a flick of her wrist, the remaining sword light changed direction, trying to bypass the lightning storm and strike Max from behind, but Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body had already captured the shift in space and energy before the attack could reach him.
Lightning flashed beneath his feet.
Max disappeared.
When he reappeared, he was already above Selene.
Dragonheart descended with seven-colored lightning wrapped around its blade.
Selene reacted instantly.

A golden shield shaped like a lotus bloomed above her head, each petal made of condensed Heavenly Luminance power. Max’s sword slammed into the shield, and the collision created a shockwave that spread across the base of the Witch God Tree. The lotus shield trembled violently, several petals cracking under the combined force of Dragonheart and Divine King Punishment, but it did not break immediately.
Selene moved back, her expression finally becoming serious.
"You have more than one Pseudo Cosmic Path," she said coldly.
Max’s gaze remained calm. "You noticed quickly."

chapters.title: Chapter 1779: Storm King’s Verdict!
paragraphs: Selene’s eyes flashed. "Do not think that makes you invincible."

Her golden crown brightened, and a pair of radiant wings unfolded behind her. The wings were vast, elegant, and filled with golden runes, and the moment they appeared, Selene’s speed increased tremendously. She vanished from her original position and appeared to Max’s right, releasing a palm strike filled with condensed light.
"Solar Luminance Palm."
The palm seemed to carry a small sun inside it.
Max turned and met it with a slash of lightning.
Boom!

The palm exploded into fragments of golden light, but Selene had already moved again. She appeared above him this time, both hands forming a seal as a huge golden wheel appeared behind her. The wheel rotated with terrifying speed, and every rotation released blades of light that cut toward Max from dozens of directions.
"Heavenly Wheel of Radiant Execution."

The attack was far stronger than the sword rain. The golden wheel suppressed the battlefield, split the air, and created a storm of light blades so dense that it seemed impossible to avoid. The second faction elves watching from the side regained some confidence when they saw it, because this was one of Selene’s true combat techniques, and many geniuses of the same realm had fallen beneath it.
Max stood in the center of the light blade storm.
Seven-colored lightning rose around him like a divine punishment barrier.
The light blades struck the lightning.
One after another, they shattered.

Max lifted Dragonheart and slashed upward. A seven-colored lightning arc tore through the air, splitting the Heavenly Wheel of Radiant Execution from the center. The golden wheel cracked, trembled, and then exploded into a shower of light fragments.
Selene’s expression changed again.
Max did not let the chance pass.

Lightning erupted beneath his feet, and his figure rushed forward with terrifying speed. He appeared in front of Selene and thrust Dragonheart straight toward her chest. Selene’s golden wings folded in front of her, forming a layered defense, while her crown released a circle of light that pushed outward like a wave.
Max’s sword pierced through the first layer.
Then the second.
Then the third.

Selene gritted her teeth, and the halo behind her expanded suddenly. A mirror of light appeared between them, and Max’s sword struck the mirror with a thunderous sound. The mirror cracked but managed to divert his thrust slightly, causing Dragonheart to pass beside Selene’s shoulder instead of through her heart.
Even so, the lightning wrapped around the blade grazed her arm.

Selene’s sleeve was instantly destroyed, and a thin wound appeared on her fair skin. Seven-colored lightning crawled over the wound like living punishment, causing her bloodline power to tremble slightly before she forcefully dispersed it.
The second faction elves stared in disbelief.
The Divine Daughter had been injured.
Even if it was only a small wound, it was still enough to shake them.
Seraphine’s face became ugly. "Impossible..."
Fin’s eyes flickered with fear again. "He can actually pressure Selene."
Selene’s expression turned colder than before.

The wound was not serious, but the meaning behind it was unacceptable. She had been trained by the Bloodline Hall, personally guided by powerful ancestors, and recognized as the Divine Daughter of the second faction.

Her Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline was extremely pure, and among the younger generation of the elf race, very few could force her into danger. Yet Max had not only blocked her techniques, but had taken the initiative to attack and wounded her.
"You are stronger than I expected," Selene said softly.
Max pointed Dragonheart at her. "You are weaker than I expected."
The words made the golden light around Selene flare violently.
"Do not get arrogant."

Her bloodline power erupted to a new level, and the crown above her head transformed into a full divine diadem. Golden armor formed over her body, covering her arms, shoulders, chest, and legs with radiant plates carved from light itself.
Behind her, a giant phantom of a heavenly elf queen appeared, holding a spear of pure golden radiance. The aura that descended from that phantom made Caroline’s face turn grave.
Caroline said in a low voice, "That is one of the second faction’s strongest bloodline techniques. Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar."
Selene raised her hand, and the phantom behind her raised the golden spear.
The spear became enormous, stretching from the ground to the sky, and every inch of it burned with bloodline suppression and sacred destruction.
"Heavenly Luminance, Queen’s Divine Spear."
The spear descended toward Max.
The pressure was terrifying.

The ground beneath Max cracked even before the attack arrived, and the golden light sealed the surrounding space to prevent him from dodging. It was clear that Selene had truly begun using her full power. She was not holding back, and the strength she displayed made everyone understand why she had the right to be called the Divine Daughter of the second faction.
Max smiled faintly for the first time since the battle began.
"Not bad."
The divine throne of seven-colored lightning behind him became clearer.

Thunderclouds gathered above the battlefield, and the seven colors of lightning condensed into a massive spear of punishment in Max’s hand. It was not a weapon made from metal, but from storm authority and destructive lightning. He raised it toward the descending golden spear, and the aura around him became as majestic as a ruler announcing punishment to the heavens.
"Divine King Punishment, Storm King’s Verdict."
The seven-colored lightning spear shot upward.
The two spears collided above the battlefield.
The explosion shook the base of the Witch God Tree.

Golden light and seven-colored lightning swallowed everything. The huge roots beneath the battlefield cracked open, the surrounding formations trembled, and many second faction elves were forced to retreat again and again.

Rosaline’s followers raised defensive barriers. Morgana waved her hand and formed a starry curtain before herself. Kaiden distorted the space around him. Orion stood still and let the shockwave crash against his body, his grin growing wider.
In the center of the explosion, Selene pressed down with all her strength.
Max pushed upward with Divine King Punishment.
For several breaths, the two powers seemed evenly matched.
Then the punishment lightning began to devour the golden radiance.
Crack!
The Queen’s Divine Spear cracked.
Selene’s pupils narrowed.

The seven-colored lightning spread across the golden spear like divine judgment, destroying its structure from within. The Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar behind Selene trembled violently as the spear broke apart, and when the final surge of lightning erupted, the golden spear shattered completely.
Selene was thrown backward.
Her feet slid across the ground, leaving two long marks on the giant root beneath her.
The battlefield went silent for a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Chapter 1780: Furious Selene!
paragraphs: Then Selene lifted her head, and her eyes were no longer calm.
She was furious.
But more than that, she was shaken.

Max had not used the Emotion Severing Path. He had not activated all of his hidden cards. He had only used this seven-colored lightning Pseudo Cosmic Path, yet it had suppressed every light-based attack she had released so far. Her sword rain, her lotus shield, her radiant palm, her heavenly wheel, her light mirror, and even the Queen’s Divine Spear had all failed to defeat him.
Selene clenched her hands, and the golden bloodline light around her burned even brighter.
Max stepped forward again.
The seven-colored lightning circled him, his dark hair moving wildly in the storm, Dragonheart in his hand reflecting both golden light and thunder.

He had to admit Selene was strong. She was not like Seraphine or Fin. She reacted faster, defended better, attacked with greater precision, and her Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline gave her an extremely stable foundation. If any other genius at her level faced her, they might truly be crushed by her divine light.
But Max was also strong.
And against the second faction, he would not yield even one step.
Selene raised both hands.

The golden halo behind her split into twelve smaller halos, each one forming a different radiant weapon: sword, spear, bow, chain, shield, axe, whip, lance, wheel, blade, hammer, and staff. At the same time, the Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar behind her became more solid, and countless golden runes spread across the battlefield like a sacred formation.
"Twelve Luminance Edicts."
The twelve weapons descended together.

Each weapon carried a different kind of light-based power. The sword cut, the spear pierced, the bow shot, the chain bound, the shield suppressed, the axe split, the whip restrained, the lance broke defenses, the wheel shredded, the blade erased, the hammer crushed, and the staff sealed. Together, they formed a terrifying all-directional attack that showed the true depth of Selene’s inheritance.
Max raised Dragonheart.
Seven-colored lightning gathered into his sword.
"Divine King Punishment, Thousand Thunder Judgments."
He slashed.
One slash became ten.
Ten became a hundred.
A hundred became a thousand.

Seven-colored lightning sword lights filled the battlefield, clashing against the twelve radiant weapons in a storm of divine destruction. Every collision created a thunderous explosion. Every destroyed weapon released a burst of golden light. Every shattered lightning arc rebounded into the sky and formed new thunderbolts that descended again under Max’s control.
Selene moved through the storm with terrifying grace, her golden wings carrying her across the battlefield as she continuously formed new weapons of light.
Max moved just as quickly, using the Vein of Speed faintly beneath the surface of his body while letting Divine King Punishment dominate the clash.
He attacked when Selene formed her next seal.
He slashed when her defense shifted.
He appeared above her when her attention moved to the lightning storm, forcing her to raise three halos to block Dragonheart.
She countered with a beam of Heavenly Luminance light aimed directly at his chest.
Max cut it apart and sent a seven-colored lightning palm toward her shoulder.
Selene dodged by turning into light and reappeared behind him with a golden blade.
Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body sensed the movement and made him turn before the blade could land.
Their attacks collided again.
Boom!
The entire base of the Witch God Tree became their battlefield.
Golden radiance and seven-colored lightning filled the sky.
The second faction elves watched with shocked eyes, because Selene was displaying power worthy of the Divine Daughter, yet Max was still matching her directly.

Caroline watched with a complicated expression, because the golden light used by Selene came from the same elven bloodline system that had once belonged to her sister’s lineage, but in front of Max’s seven-colored lightning, that light was repeatedly being broken.

Rosaline watched without blinking, realizing that the terrifying sword aura was not the only mystery surrounding Max. Morgana smiled less and less, her eyes full of calculation. Kaiden remained silent, but his gaze stayed fixed on Max’s spatial movements. Orion laughed several times, clearly enjoying the sight of two monsters colliding beneath the Witch God Tree.
The battle grew fiercer.

Selene was truly worthy of being called the Divine Daughter of the elven race’s second faction. Every time Max broke one technique, she revealed another. Every time his lightning suppressed her light, she refined her control and struck from another angle. Her combat sense was sharp, her bloodline was pure, her techniques were vast, and her foundation was strong enough that even after multiple clashes, her aura did not collapse.
But Max was not inferior.

His Divine King Punishment was too destructive. The seven-colored lightning did not merely collide with Selene’s light. It punished it. It broke through it. It carried the essence of the Storm King’s Inheritance and the destructive nature of seven-colored lightning, making every strike feel like judgment from a divine thunder ruler.

Whenever Selene’s light tried to suppress him, his lightning tore through the suppression. Whenever her bloodline tried to purify his power, his punishment lightning blasted apart the purification. Whenever she formed a sacred domain of light, Max shattered it with one storm-charged slash.
After dozens of exchanges, Selene finally retreated into the air, breathing slightly harder than before.
Max stood below her, still calm, seven-colored lightning wrapping around him like a storm cloak.
Neither of them had truly fallen.
Neither of them had been decisively defeated.
But everyone could see that Selene had used many powerful light-based techniques, while Max had used only one Pseudo Cosmic Path to answer all of them.
Divine King Punishment.
The name now felt carved into the battlefield itself.
Selene stared down at Max, her golden eyes filled with anger, caution, and something she did not want to admit.
Pressure.
Max looked up at her and smiled faintly.
"Is that all the Divine Daughter can do?"
The seven-colored lightning behind him roared again, and the divine thunder throne became even more imposing.
Selene’s face turned cold, and her golden aura surged once more.
The battle was far from over.

Selene floated in the air, golden light pouring from her body like a divine tide, while Max stood below her wrapped in seven-colored lightning, Dragonheart in hand, his Divine King Punishment still roaring like a heavenly storm around him.

The battlefield had already been shaken again and again by their clash. Giant roots at the base of the Witch God Tree were cracked open, nearby stone ridges had collapsed, and the space between them was still filled with scattered sparks of golden radiance and seven-colored lightning.
Selene’s expression was colder than ever, while Max’s remained calm and faintly sharp, as if he was still not pressured enough by everything she had shown so far.
That calmness was the final thing Selene could no longer endure.
She slowly raised both hands.
The halo behind her began to tremble.

The divine diadem above her head dissolved into countless strands of golden light, and those strands did not scatter aimlessly. Instead, they gathered behind her into a huge circular formation that looked like a sacred sun wheel mixed with an ancient heavenly gate.

The very moment it began to form, the entire base of the Witch God Tree grew heavy. The second faction elves immediately showed signs of awe, Rosaline’s expression turned more serious, Morgana’s purple eyes flickered faintly, Kaiden looked up with a slightly sharper gaze, and even Orion’s grin faded a little as he realized that Selene was finally about to reveal her true path.
Caroline’s face changed sharply.
"Max," she called out, her voice tense, "be careful. She is going to use her Pseudo Cosmic Path."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly, but he did not look back.

chapters.title: Chapter 1781: A Sneak Attack
paragraphs: Caroline continued quickly, because she knew that once Selene’s path fully unfolded, there might not be another moment to speak. "Her Pseudo Cosmic Path is said to be one of the strongest paths among the younger generation of the second faction. Even the ancestors treated it very seriously. The only reason she does not use it freely is because it consumes too much of her power. She can only sustain it for a short period of time before it drains her energy rapidly."
Nancy’s face became grave.
Jessica and the other third faction elves swallowed hard.
If even Caroline, someone who had once belonged to the heart of the elven royal line, said that Selene’s path was one of the strongest, then it was not something to underestimate.
Max’s eyes remained fixed on Selene.
"Then she should use it now," he said calmly.
Selene heard his words.
A cold smile touched her lips.
"Do not regret asking for this."
The sacred sun wheel behind her fully opened.
Then her Pseudo Cosmic Path descended.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path... Heavenly Luminance Genesis."
The moment the name fell, the world seemed to brighten.

A domain of pure golden-white radiance unfolded behind Selene, vast and grand like the birth of a divine heaven. Within that path, one could see countless layers of sacred palaces, endless rivers of luminance, golden suns rising and falling, and divine chains of law crossing the sky.
It did not feel like an ordinary path built on battle intent alone. It felt like the beginning of a holy kingdom, a genesis light capable of birthing order, authority, and divine suppression.
The air trembled.
The ground groaned.

Max’s seven-colored lightning domain was still violent and majestic, but for the first time in this battle, it encountered a radiance so pure and so overwhelmingly structured that even Divine King Punishment seemed to meet an equal in authority.
Selene’s golden hair floated upward.
Her eyes turned completely radiant, no longer showing ordinary pupils but only divine light.
The halo behind her dissolved into that Genesis Path, and in the center of the vast heavenly radiance, a single weapon slowly formed in her hands.
It was a spear.
A spear of blinding white-gold light.

But unlike her previous Queen’s Divine Spear, this weapon did not merely contain radiant bloodline power. It contained the essence of her Pseudo Cosmic Path itself. Every inch of the spear was wrapped in the beginning and order of her Heavenly Luminance Genesis.
Merely looking at it made many weaker observers feel their minds tremble, as though their thoughts were being purified and suppressed by something higher.
Seraphine’s face filled with excitement. "Divine Daughter is finally serious."
Fin also looked relieved. "This time he should fall."
Rosaline stared without blinking.
Morgana’s smile became thin and unreadable.
Kaiden remained silent.
Orion crossed his arms more tightly and focused harder.
Selene raised the spear.
"Heavenly Luminance Genesis, Spear of First Dawn."
The giant Genesis domain behind her condensed.
Palaces of light, rivers of radiance, and suns of holy brilliance all collapsed inward toward that spear, turning it into the embodiment of beginning light. Then Selene thrust it downward at Max.
The spear descended.
Everything in its path was erased.
The air became light.
The storm around Max was split open.

The giant roots beneath the battlefield were torn apart as the attack fell with unstoppable authority. This was not just an attack of power. It was an attack carrying origin, suppression, order, and the overwhelming sanctity of Selene’s strongest path.
Caroline’s face turned pale.
"That attack..."
Even she had not expected Selene to use her strongest path so decisively.
But Max did not retreat.

The moment the Spear of First Dawn descended, Max’s eyes became colder, and his seven-colored lightning erupted again. Divine King Punishment roared around him, the thunder throne behind him becoming even more imposing as he prepared to answer Selene’s strongest path head-on. Lightning condensed around Dragonheart, and the destructive, punishing essence of his path gathered to an extreme.
He was ready to counter.
He was ready to destroy Selene together with her Heavenly Luminance Genesis.
But just as Max was about to move, something unexpected happened.
The ground beneath him exploded.

Countless roots of the Witch God Tree burst out from below like living serpents. They moved too suddenly, too quietly, and too unnaturally. Their timing was perfect, striking at the exact instant all of Max’s attention had been focused upward on Selene’s descending Pseudo Cosmic Path attack.

Even with his Dimensional Sovereign Body, the interference came too abruptly and from too close. Before he could completely shift away, the giant roots wrapped around his legs, his waist, his sword arm, and his other shoulder, binding him in place.
Max’s eyes changed instantly.
This sneak attack had come completely out of nowhere.
For the briefest moment, even he was caught off guard.
Caroline gasped. "Max!"
Jessica’s face turned pale. Nancy’s expression changed sharply.
Orion’s eyes widened slightly.
Kaiden’s gaze became deeper.
Rosaline’s brows furrowed.
And then everyone’s eyes turned toward one person.
Morgana Starveil.

The witch stood at the edge of the battlefield with one hand slightly raised, and around her fingers, faint violet star-charms were revolving slowly. Her expression remained graceful and calm, but the meaning of what had happened was clear to everyone present.
The roots of the Witch God Tree had not acted on their own. They had been controlled, guided, or awakened by her witchcraft.
Even Selene seemed momentarily surprised by the timing, but she did not stop her attack.
If Max was bound, then better.
The Spear of First Dawn descended completely.
Max was still restricted.
And in the next instant, Selene’s full-powered attack landed on him while he was completely defenseless.
Boom!
The explosion was world-shaking.

Golden-white radiance swallowed the battlefield whole. The entire base of the Witch God Tree trembled violently, countless nearby roots were blown apart, and the force of the clash spread outward in a ring of destructive light that forced even the surrounding observers to retreat or raise defenses.

The second faction elves stumbled backward, Rosaline’s group activated barriers, Kaiden distorted the incoming shockwave, Morgana raised a curtain of purple starlight before herself, and Orion only planted his feet harder as the explosion crashed into him with a wide grin.
The third faction elves were horrified.
Caroline nearly stepped forward on instinct, but Jessica and Nancy stopped her.
Dust, light, shattered bark, and broken roots filled the battlefield.
For several breaths, no one could see anything.
Seraphine’s face lit up. "He took it head-on while restricted."
Fin laughed in relief. "This time there is no way he survived that without heavy injuries."
Selene remained in the air, breathing slightly harder now.
Caroline’s warning had been true.

Using Heavenly Luminance Genesis drained her power quickly. Even though she stood straight, there was a faint instability in her aura now, and the vast radiance behind her had already dimmed somewhat after unleashing that terrifying attack.

Yet in her eyes, there was still confidence. Max had been restrained at the critical moment. Her full-powered strike had landed directly. Even if he was absurdly strong, there was no reason for him to emerge unscathed from that.
The battlefield slowly began to clear.
The light faded.
The dust settled.
And then everyone saw him.
Max was still standing in the center of the ruined battlefield.

The roots binding him had already been shattered, broken into blackened fragments around his feet. His body had not been pierced. His flesh had not been burned. His clothes were torn and partly destroyed from the explosion, but beneath them, his body was now covered in golden-black dragon scales from head to toe.
Every scale gleamed with a terrifying luster.
They were neither purely golden nor purely black, but a fusion of both, carrying an ancient, noble, and chaotic aura at the same time.

The remaining traces of Selene’s Genesis light were still crawling across those scales, but they could not penetrate them at all. Instead, the light slid away or shattered apart as though it had struck the body of an ancient dragon king rather than a human cultivator.
For a moment, no one spoke.
Caroline’s eyes widened.
Jessica looked stunned.
Nancy slowly exhaled, though the shock in her face remained.
Seraphine’s expression froze.
Fin’s smile vanished.
Rosaline’s pupils narrowed.
Kaiden’s gaze became serious.
Orion let out a low whistle.
Even Morgana’s calm smile wavered slightly.
At the center of it all, Max slowly raised his head.

Golden-black scales covered his face and neck, leaving only his eyes fully visible, and those eyes were now colder than before. Lightning still coiled around him. Dragonheart remained in his hand. The small cursed eye clung to his left shoulder as if even the Witch’s mark was watching in silence.
Max looked first at Selene.
Then his gaze slowly moved toward Morgana.
His voice was calm, but terrifying.
"So," he said softly, "that is how you want to play."

chapters.title: Chapter 1782: Shameless Morgana!
paragraphs: "So, what of it?" Morgana sneered.
Her earlier graceful smile had disappeared, and what remained on her beautiful face was a cold, mocking expression that made the charm around her feel poisonous.

The small crystal charms floating around her fingers spun slowly, and faint violet threads connected them to the roots of the Witch God Tree beneath the battlefield, revealing that her interference had not been accidental at all.

She had been waiting. She had watched Max and Selene clash, waited until Selene released her strongest Pseudo Cosmic Path, waited until Max was about to counterattack, and only then had she chosen the most disgusting moment to strike from the shadows.
"This is a battle royale," Morgana continued, her voice carrying no shame at all. "You did not expect us to be mere spectators, did you?"
Her words made the expressions of many people change.

Even some of the second faction elves looked at her with strange eyes. They had been Max’s enemies from the beginning, so they naturally wanted him dead, but even they had not expected Morgana, who had introduced herself with such elegance and had claimed to be only curious about the Witch’s curse mark, to interfere so suddenly in another person’s duel.

Her timing had been too vicious. She had not challenged Max openly. She had not even attacked him directly. She had used the roots of the Witch God Tree to bind him from below when his attention was fully occupied by Selene’s strongest attack, deliberately trying to make him take that blow without defense.
Caroline’s eyes turned cold with anger. "Shameless."
Jessica clenched her sword. "You call that battle? You hid behind the Witch God Tree and stabbed from the dark like a rat."
Morgana glanced at Jessica, then smiled with cruel amusement. "A rat that succeeds is still alive. A proud fool who fails is still dead. Which one do you think matters more in this conference?"
Jessica’s face darkened.
Caroline looked at Morgana with undisguised disgust. "Stellar Templar is one of the seven strongest first-rate forces of the Divine Realm. Is this how its strongest genius conducts herself?"

Morgana laughed softly, and that laugh made her even more hateful than if she had simply been cruel. There was no guilt in it. There was no trace of embarrassment. Instead, she looked almost entertained by their anger, as if the disgust of others was another form of applause.

"Please, do not speak to me about honor," Morgana said lightly. "Honor is a word used by people who need others to admire the way they lose. I prefer winning. If binding him for a moment gives me a chance to see whether Selene’s strongest attack can break his body, then why would I not do it?"
Her purple eyes moved back to Max, and a thin smile appeared on her lips.
"Besides, he did not die. So why are all of you so angry?"
That sentence made the atmosphere even colder.
Even Rosaline frowned slightly.
Kaiden’s gaze toward Morgana became more distant.
Orion’s smile vanished for the first time, and he looked at the witch with clear displeasure. "You really are unpleasant."
Morgana turned her head slightly and smiled at him. "Unpleasant people live longer, Orion."
Orion snorted coldly. "Not always."

Selene, who had just used Heavenly Luminance Genesis and was still recovering from the drain, looked at Morgana with a complicated expression. Although Morgana’s interference had helped her attack land on Max, even Selene did not enjoy the feeling of having her duel dirtied by someone else’s trick. Yet she did not speak against it either.
In a battle royale, results mattered, and if Max had truly been injured by that attack, Selene would not have refused the advantage.
Max looked at Morgana silently.

The golden-black dragon scales covering his body gleamed faintly, and the seven-colored lightning around him had become quieter, but that quietness was more dangerous than the storm from before. His eyes were calm, yet the calmness now carried a weight that made the air around him feel sharper.
Then he nodded his head.
"Fair."
Morgana raised an eyebrow.
Max continued calmly, "This is indeed a battle royale, and your actions are justified."
For a brief moment, Morgana’s smile widened.

She seemed to think Max had accepted her logic, or perhaps she thought he was trying to suppress his anger because too many strong people were present. Her expression became even more mocking, and the violet charms around her fingers revolved lazily as if she was already preparing another trick.
But Max’s next words made her smile pause.
"Since your actions are justified," Max said softly, "then whatever I do to you next is also justified."
The battlefield fell silent.
Morgana’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Max slowly turned his body toward her.

The broken roots around his feet burned away under black flames, and the golden-black dragon scales covering him released a deep draconic pressure that spread across the base of the Witch God Tree. The little cursed eye on his left shoulder blinked once, its pupil turning toward Morgana as if even the Witch’s mark was waiting to see what he would do.
Morgana’s smile did not fully disappear, but a trace of caution entered her eyes.
"Oh?" she said, still trying to sound amused. "Are you planning to attack me now while Selene is still standing before you?"
Max looked at her.
"You joined the battle first."
Morgana’s fingers twitched slightly.

Max continued, his voice calm and cold. "You did not interfere to test me. You waited for the worst possible moment and tried to make someone else’s strongest attack land while I was bound. If my defense had been weaker, Caroline and the others would now be watching my body torn apart, and you would still be smiling as if you had done something clever."
Caroline’s expression tightened.
Nancy’s eyes became cold.
Jessica glared at Morgana with hatred.

Morgana’s expression finally changed a little because Max had described her intention perfectly. She had not cared whether he died. She had not cared whether it was fair. She had wanted to see his secrets, and if he died in the process, then that would only mean he had not been worth her attention.
Max took one step toward her.
The ground beneath his foot cracked.
"So I will remember you, Morgana Starveil."
His voice was still calm, but everyone could hear the threat inside it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1783: Dealing with Selene First!
paragraphs: Max then turned to look at Selene.

The golden radiance around her was still bright, and the vast image of Heavenly Luminance Genesis had not fully vanished behind her, but anyone with sharp eyes could already see the truth. The sacred palaces of light in her Pseudo Cosmic Path were flickering.

The golden rivers flowing through the radiant domain were breaking apart into unstable fragments. Even the divine sun wheel behind her had become dimmer than before, and the Spear of First Dawn she had unleashed had drained far more of her strength than she wanted others to notice.
Max looked at her calmly.
"I won, right?"
Selene’s eyes turned colder.

Max continued before she could answer, his voice spreading clearly across the base of the Witch God Tree. "You are already trembling from the use of your Pseudo Cosmic Path. And as Caroline said, you cannot maintain this form for too long. You are barely holding on."
The moment those words came out, many people finally noticed Selene’s condition.
Her fingers were indeed trembling slightly. Her breathing had become heavier, and although she stood straight with the pride of the Divine Daughter, her aura was no longer as stable as before.

The Pseudo Cosmic Path of Heavenly Luminance Genesis was terrifyingly powerful, but that power came at an equally terrifying cost. It could overwhelm most enemies in a short period of time, yet if the first few attacks failed to secure victory, the burden would turn against Selene herself.
Caroline’s expression became serious. "He is right. Her path is weakening."
Seraphine’s face changed. "Divine Daughter..."
Fin’s expression also became ugly, because the confidence he had felt when Selene unleashed her strongest path had disappeared the moment Max emerged from the dust without a single injury.

Even after being bound by the roots of the Witch God Tree and struck directly by Selene’s strongest attack, Max was still standing there unharmed, covered in golden-black dragon scales, while Selene was the one who had exhausted a great amount of power.
Selene gritted her teeth.
"Do not act as if this is over."

Her voice was cold, but there was now a trace of strain hidden inside it. She raised both hands again, and the weakened Heavenly Luminance Genesis behind her trembled violently as she forcefully tried to gather another wave of golden-white radiance.

The twelve halos around her reappeared, though they were no longer as solid as before, and sacred weapons of light began to form inside them once more. Even in her weakened state, Selene still refused to retreat.

She was the Divine Daughter of the second faction. She had been trained by the Bloodline Hall and the ancestors. She could not accept defeat before so many geniuses, especially not against Caelira’s son.
Max looked at her and shook his head slightly.
"You should have stopped."
Selene’s eyes flashed with anger. "I have not lost."
"Then I will make it clearer."
Just as Max said those words, his Vein of Speed came to life.
The air around him twisted.
The next instant, his figure vanished from where he stood.
Selene’s pupils contracted.
Fast.
Too fast.

Even with her Heavenly Luminance Genesis still active, even with her golden eyes strengthened by her royal bloodline, she could barely catch the trace of Max’s movement. One moment he was standing several dozen meters away, and in the next, he had appeared right before her, the golden-black scales on his body reflecting the dim light of her collapsing Pseudo Cosmic Path.

His speed was not just ordinary movement. It was the explosive burst of the Vein of Speed combined with his terrifying physical foundation, making him cross the distance like a dragon tearing through space.
Selene reacted instantly.
Despite her shock, her combat instinct was worthy of the Divine Daughter.

A radiant shield formed in front of her chest. Then a second shield appeared. Then a third. Golden-white light surged around her, forming overlapping barriers shaped like divine lotus petals, sacred mirrors, and bloodline runic circles. The remnants of Heavenly Luminance Genesis also gathered around her body, trying to turn the space between her and Max into a protected domain of light.
But Max was faster.
The moment he appeared before her, the Vein of Strength awakened inside his body.
Boom!
His muscles tightened beneath the golden-black dragon scales, and the pressure released from his flesh alone caused the light around Selene to shake violently.

Then five thousand Draconic Essences erupted through him at the same time, pouring into his arm like the condensed might of an ancient dragon. The power gathered in his fist was devastating, heavy, and brutally simple, without the elegance of sword arts or the mystic complexity of Pseudo Cosmic Paths.
It was pure destruction.
Selene’s expression changed completely.
"Wait..."
Max punched.
Bang!
His fist slammed into Selene’s defensive shield.
The first radiant barrier exploded instantly.
The second shattered before it could even release its full power.
The third cracked apart like thin glass beneath a mountain’s weight.

The divine lotus petals broke. The sacred mirrors burst. The bloodline runic circles collapsed one after another, and the remaining light of Heavenly Luminance Genesis was crushed under the overwhelming combination of the Vein of Strength and five thousand Draconic Essences.
Selene’s eyes widened in disbelief as every defense she had raised was destroyed in a single instant.
Then Max’s fist reached her.
The impact struck her body head-on.
For a fraction of a second, the entire battlefield became silent.

Selene’s golden eyes stared at Max from only a few inches away, still filled with shock, unwillingness, and disbelief. She had never imagined that after revealing Heavenly Luminance Genesis, after using one of the strongest Pseudo Cosmic Paths of the second faction, after forcing Max to reveal his dragon scales, she would be taken out by one punch.
But Max’s power had already passed through every defense she possessed, and there was nothing left to protect her.
Her body shattered into light.
Golden cracks spread across her form.

Then, with a burst of radiant fragments, Selene Vaeloria, the Divine Daughter of the second faction, disappeared from the battlefield and turned into a dense stream of Killing Points that surged toward Max.
The golden light vanished.
Her Heavenly Luminance Genesis collapsed.

The sacred palaces, divine rivers, sun wheel, and radiant halos all broke apart like an illusion being destroyed by force, leaving only scattered motes of light drifting through the air before they faded completely.
For a long moment, no one spoke.
The second faction elves stared blankly at the empty place where Selene had stood.
Seraphine’s face turned deathly pale.
Fin took an unconscious step back.
Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the third faction elves were equally stunned, even though they had already seen Max do impossible things inside Witch God Valley.

This was different. Selene was not Lumine. She was not Arnold. She was not even Seraphine or Fin. She was the Divine Daughter, one of the strongest geniuses of the second faction, yet Max had ended her the moment he chose to stop playing defense.
Rosaline’s eyes narrowed deeply.
Morgana’s expression became much more serious.
Kaiden Voidmere remained silent, but the space around him rippled once.
Orion Starfall let out a slow breath, and the excitement in his eyes grew even stronger.
At the center of everyone’s gaze, Max slowly lowered his fist.

The golden-black dragon scales still covered his body, and faint seven-colored lightning flickered around him. The small cursed eye attached to his left shoulder blinked silently, as if it too had witnessed the fall of the Divine Daughter.
Dragonheart remained in his other hand, but he had not even needed to use it to finish Selene.

chapters.title: Chapter 1784: Three Moves to Morgana!
paragraphs: The entire base of the Witch God Tree fell into a silence so heavy that even the cursed wind seemed to stop moving.
Selene was gone.

The Divine Daughter of the second faction, the golden-haired genius trained by the Bloodline Hall and guided by the ancestors, the young woman who had unleashed the terrifying Pseudo Cosmic Path known as Heavenly Luminance Genesis, had been destroyed by a single punch after Max decided to close the distance.

It had not been a desperate struggle where both sides exhausted everything. Max had simply used the Vein of Speed to appear before her, activated the Vein of Strength, poured five thousand Draconic Essences into his fist, and shattered her defenses along with her body.

Rosaline stared at the empty space where Selene had disappeared, and for the first time since arriving at the base of the Witch God Tree, her calm expression showed clear shock. She had known Max was dangerous.
She had come here precisely because of the terrifying sword aura he had left behind near the neutral city, but seeing him kill Selene in one punch was something else entirely.

Selene was not some unknown genius. She was one of the strongest names among the younger generation of the elven race, and even Rosaline would have needed to treat her seriously if they fought. Yet Max had ended her after enduring her strongest Pseudo Cosmic Path attack without injury.
The young man standing beside Rosaline also looked stunned. "Princess... he killed Selene Vaeloria."
Rosaline did not answer immediately.
Her gaze remained fixed on Max’s golden-black dragon scales, then shifted to the faint seven-colored lightning still flickering around him, then finally moved to Dragonheart in his other hand.

The strange thing was that Max had still not released the sword aura that had originally drawn her here. Even after fighting Selene, even after being ambushed by Morgana, even after killing the Divine Daughter, he had relied on other powers.
That realization made Rosaline’s shock turn into something deeper.
’He still has not used that sword path,’ Rosaline thought, her eyes narrowing slightly. ’Just how many hidden cards does he have?’
Morgana Starveil was also silent.

Her earlier mocking smile had vanished after Selene’s death. The witch from Stellar Templar stared at Max with narrowed purple eyes, and although she quickly regained her composure, the brief stiffness in her expression had already revealed that she had not expected Selene to fall so suddenly.
Kaiden Voidmere’s gaze remained calm, but the space around him rippled faintly, as if his body had instinctively reacted to Max’s burst of speed.

Orion Starfall, on the other hand, looked excited, but even his excitement was mixed with caution now. Max had just shown that if he wanted to end a fight quickly, his close-range killing power was terrifying.
The second faction elves were in even worse condition.

Seraphine’s face had become pale to the point of looking bloodless. Fin no longer had any desire to speak. The other elves stared at Max as if looking at a monster in human form, because the person they had trusted the most, the person they believed could suppress Max, had been turned into Killing Points before their eyes.
The confidence created by their numbers, formations, and bloodline suppression talismans cracked apart at that moment.
Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the third faction elves were equally shaken, but their shock carried a completely different emotion.
Max did not pay attention to the silence around him.
He slowly turned his head.
His gaze moved away from the place where Selene had died and landed on Morgana Starveil. "Let us finish what you started, shall we?"
Morgana heard him and immediately sneered.
"Humph, do you really think if you can handle Selene, you can also kill me?" Morgana said, her voice sharp with cold arrogance. "You have got it all wrong."
Her words broke the silence and made many people look at her.

Even after seeing Selene die, Morgana still did not step back. Violet starlight gathered around her body, and the crystal charms floating beside her began spinning faster, forming faint circles of witchcraft power around her.
Unlike Selene, who fought with open radiance and overwhelming bloodline power, Morgana’s strength was strange, hidden, and poisonous.

She was a witch from Stellar Templar, one of the seven strongest first-rate forces of the Divine Realm, and her methods were not meant to be fair, beautiful, or direct. They were meant to make enemies die without understanding how they had been trapped.
Max smiled lightly.
"If it were the real world, I would have surely killed you by now in pure rage," he said calmly. "I hate sneak attackers the most."
Morgana’s eyes narrowed.
The air around her became colder.
Max continued arrogantly, "But since this is a battle royale, I will allow you three moves."
The moment those words came out, the expressions of everyone present changed again.
Rosaline’s pupils tightened slightly.
Caroline was stunned.
Nancy looked at Max with surprise.
Orion Starfall’s eyes widened, then he suddenly laughed. "Three moves? He is even more arrogant than I thought."
Kaiden Voidmere remained expressionless, but his gaze became much sharper.
Morgana stared at Max for a moment, then her lips curled into a cold smile. "You will allow me three moves?"

Her voice was filled with disbelief and mockery, but beneath that mockery, a trace of anger had clearly appeared. She was Morgana Starveil, one of the strongest geniuses of Stellar Templar. People feared her curses, her witchcraft, her fate-reading, and her ability to control a battlefield from the shadows. Yet Max was speaking as if she were someone he could casually test, tolerate, and then cut down whenever he pleased.
Max raised Dragonheart slightly.

The seven-colored lightning around him slowly faded, and in its place, a quieter and more terrifying sword aura began to stir. It was not fully released yet, but the moment it appeared, Rosaline’s expression changed. She recognized it. This was the very aura that had made her come all the way here.
Max looked at Morgana and spoke in an even calmer voice.
"If you cannot kill me in three moves, my sword will sever your existence in two."
The battlefield went completely still.
The word sever made Seraphine and Fin instinctively tremble.
They had felt that sword path before. They knew what it meant. They have experienced it themselves. No matter how hard they tried, they simply couldn’t get past the severing power of Max’s sword.
Morgana’s smile stiffened for a heartbeat.
Then her expression turned cold and hateful.
"You are truly courting death, Max Morgan."
Max’s smile did not disappear.
"First move," he said.
Morgana’s eyes flashed with killing intent.
The violet charms around her body suddenly stopped spinning.

Then, one by one, they cracked open, releasing threads of purple starlight that spread into the air like a spiderweb woven from fate and curse power. At the same time, the roots beneath the Witch God Tree trembled again, and faint witch runes appeared across the ground around Max.
Rosaline stared at the scene with a serious expression, still shocked by Max’s arrogance but unwilling to blink.
Morgana was not Selene.
She would not fight openly if there was a more vicious way to win.
And now Max had given her three moves.
Whether that was confidence or madness, everyone was about to find out.

"Princess... he killed Selene Vaeloria."
Rosaline did not answer immediately.
Her gaze remained fixed on Max’s golden-black dragon scales, then shifted to the faint seven-colored lightning still flickering around him, then finally moved to Dragonheart in his other hand.
The strange thing was that Max had still not released the sword aura that had originally drawn her here.
Even after fighting Selene, even after being ambushed by Morgana, even after killing the Divine Daughter, he had relied on other powers.
That realization made Rosaline’s shock turn into something deeper.
’He still has not used that sword path,’ Rosaline thought, her eyes narrowing slightly. ’Just how many hidden cards does he have?’
Morgana Starveil was also silent.
Her earlier mocking smile had vanished after Selene’s death.

The witch from Stellar Templar stared at Max with narrowed purple eyes, and although she quickly regained her composure, the brief stiffness in her expression had already revealed that she had not expected Selene to fall so suddenly.
Kaiden Voidmere’s gaze remained calm, but the space around him rippled faintly, as if his body had instinctively reacted to Max’s burst of speed.
Orion Starfall, on the other hand, looked excited, but even his excitement was mixed with caution now.
Max had just shown that if he wanted to end a fight quickly, his close-range killing power was terrifying.
The second faction elves were in even worse condition.
Seraphine’s face had become pale to the point of looking bloodless.
Fin no longer had any desire to speak.

The other elves stared at Max as if looking at a monster in human form, because the person they had trusted the most, the person they believed could suppress Max, had been turned into Killing Points before their eyes.
The confidence created by their numbers, formations, and bloodline suppression talismans cracked apart at that moment.
Caroline, Jessica, Nancy, and the third faction elves were equally shaken, but their shock carried a completely different emotion.
Max did not pay attention to the silence around him.
He slowly turned his head.
His gaze moved away from the place where Selene had died and landed on Morgana Starveil.
"Let us finish what you started, shall we?"
Morgana heard him and immediately sneered.
"Humph, do you really think if you can handle Selene, you can also kill me?" Morgana said, her voice sharp with cold arrogance.
"You have got it all wrong."
Her words broke the silence and made many people look at her.
Even after seeing Selene die, Morgana still did not step back.
Violet starlight gathered around her body, and the crystal charms floating beside her began spinning faster, forming faint circles of witchcraft power around her.
Unlike Selene, who fought with open radiance and overwhelming bloodline power, Morgana’s strength was strange, hidden, and poisonous.
She was a witch from Stellar Templar, one of the seven strongest first-rate forces of the Divine Realm, and her methods were not meant to be fair, beautiful, or direct.
They were meant to make enemies die without understanding how they had been trapped.
Max smiled lightly.
"If it were the real world, I would have surely killed you by now in pure rage," he said calmly.
"I hate sneak attackers the most."
Morgana’s eyes narrowed.
The air around her became colder.
Max continued arrogantly, "But since this is a battle royale, I will allow you three moves."
The moment those words came out, the expressions of everyone present changed again.
Rosaline’s pupils tightened slightly.
Caroline was stunned.
Nancy looked at Max with surprise.
Orion Starfall’s eyes widened, then he suddenly laughed.
"Three moves?
He is even more arrogant than I thought."
Kaiden Voidmere remained expressionless, but his gaze became much sharper.
Morgana stared at Max for a moment, then her lips curled into a cold smile.
"You will allow me three moves?"
Her voice was filled with disbelief and mockery, but beneath that mockery, a trace of anger had clearly appeared.
She was Morgana Starveil, one of the strongest geniuses of Stellar Templar.
People feared her curses, her witchcraft, her fate-reading, and her ability to control a battlefield from the shadows.
Yet Max was speaking as if she were someone he could casually test, tolerate, and then cut down whenever he pleased.
Max raised Dragonheart slightly.
The seven-colored lightning around him slowly faded, and in its place, a quieter and more terrifying sword aura began to stir.
It was not fully released yet, but the moment it appeared, Rosaline’s expression changed.
She recognized it.
This was the very aura that had made her come all the way here.
Max looked at Morgana and spoke in an even calmer voice.
"If you cannot kill me in three moves, my sword will sever your existence in two."
The battlefield went completely still.
The word sever made Seraphine and Fin instinctively tremble.
They had felt that sword path before.
They knew what it meant.
They have experienced it themselves.
No matter how hard they tried, they simply couldn’t get past the severing power of Max’s sword.
Morgana’s smile stiffened for a heartbeat.
Then her expression turned cold and hateful.
"You are truly courting death, Max Morgan."
Max’s smile did not disappear.
"First move," he said.
Morgana’s eyes flashed with killing intent.
The violet charms around her body suddenly stopped spinning.
Then, one by one, they cracked open, releasing threads of purple starlight that spread into the air like a spiderweb woven from fate and curse power.
At the same time, the roots beneath the Witch God Tree trembled again, and faint witch runes appeared across the ground around Max.
Rosaline stared at the scene with a serious expression, still shocked by Max’s arrogance but unwilling to blink.
Morgana was not Selene.
She would not fight openly if there was a more vicious way to win.
And now Max had given her three moves.
Whether that was confidence or madness, everyone was about to find out.

chapters.title: Chapter 1785: Witch Attacks!
paragraphs: Morgana’s killing intent spread silently.
Unlike Selene’s golden radiance, Morgana’s power did not erupt in a bright and majestic manner. It seeped into the battlefield like poison entering water.

The violet charms around her body cracked one after another, and thin threads of purple starlight stretched outward, connecting to the roots of the Witch God Tree, the scattered pieces of cursed bark, the remnants of Selene’s shattered light, and even the dust floating in the air. In the eyes of ordinary people, it looked beautiful. In the eyes of those who understood witchcraft, it was terrifying.
A witch was most dangerous when she attacked first with preparation.
Everyone in the Divine Realm knew this.

Witches of Stellar Templar did not fight like ordinary cultivators. They did not always compete in strength, speed, or direct power. They studied curses, fate, soul marks, bloodline weaknesses, spiritual threads, and the hidden connections between people and the world around them.

Once a witch was given time to prepare, she could turn the environment into a trap, turn the enemy’s shadow into a prison, and turn the opponent’s own aura into the medium of a curse. Many geniuses who could fight warriors stronger than themselves had died miserably after allowing a witch to move first.
And Max had just given Morgana three moves.
Rosaline stared at the battlefield without blinking. "He is too confident."
Kaiden Voidmere said quietly, "Or perhaps he wants to see her strongest methods."
Orion Starfall grinned, but even he did not laugh this time. "Either way, letting Morgana Starveil attack three times without interruption is something most people would never dare to do."
Morgana heard their words and smiled coldly.
"First move."
The witch raised one finger.
The purple starlight threads around the battlefield suddenly tightened.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Thousand-Fate Needle Burial."

The moment she spoke, countless violet needles appeared in the air around Max. They were not ordinary needles made of energy. Each one was formed from curse power, star divination, and a faint thread of fate.

They did not simply aim at Max’s body. They aimed at the openings in his aura, the tiny pauses between his breaths, the flickers of energy around his joints, and even the spiritual rhythm hidden beneath his dragon scales.
The attack covered every direction, leaving no space to dodge, and more importantly, the needles seemed to adjust themselves according to Max’s movements before he even moved.
Jessica’s face turned pale. "They are predicting his movement."
Caroline’s heart tightened. "No. They are not predicting. They are using the connection between his aura and the battlefield to guide the attack."
Morgana’s smile became cruel.
The Thousand-Fate Needles descended.
Max stood still.
The golden-black dragon scales covering his body gleamed faintly, and the little cursed eye on his left shoulder blinked once as if watching the violet rain fall around him.

Max did not use Divine King Punishment. He did not use the Vein of Speed to escape. He did not even raise Dragonheart at first. He simply allowed the countless violet needles to close in until they were only a short distance away from his body.
Only then did he move.
Dragonheart turned in his hand.
A thin sword circle appeared around him.

It was not a wide slash. It was not a grand technique. It was one simple rotation of the blade, but the moment it formed, a quiet and emotionless sword intent spread outward. The violet needles entering that sword circle began to lose their direction.
Their fate threads were severed. Their curse guidance was cut. Their connection to Morgana, to the Witch God Tree, and to the battlefield itself was sliced apart cleanly.
Needle after needle fell apart.
The first layer dissolved into starlight.
The second layer shattered into dust.
The third layer collapsed before touching his scales.
Within a breath, the Thousand-Fate Needle Burial had vanished.
Max remained exactly where he was, unharmed.
Morgana’s eyes narrowed.
The surrounding geniuses stared silently.

Even Rosaline’s gaze became sharper. She had finally felt it clearly now. That terrifying sword aura, that emotionless severing power, was truly coming from Max. He had not relied on the Sword of the Sword Sovereign alone. It was his own path.
"He is strong!" Even Orion and Kaiden were a little surprised sensing Max’s sword aura.
Max lowered Dragonheart slightly.
"Second move," he said calmly.
Morgana’s expression turned colder.

She had not expected the first move to kill Max. But she had expected it to test the weakness in his defense, leave a faint curse mark, or at least force him to reveal instability. Yet Max had severed the fate-guidance of her attack so cleanly that the entire technique had collapsed before it could touch him. It was as if her witchcraft had met something that did not care about its hidden structure and simply cut the connection supporting it.
"Good," Morgana said softly. "Then let me see if you can cut this too."
She raised both hands this time.
The ground beneath Max darkened.

His shadow stretched unnaturally, then split into many black shapes. Each shadow rose from the ground like a thin, twisted figure, and every one of them had Max’s outline. The shadows opened their eyes, revealing small violet pupils similar to the witch marks Morgana used. At the same time, a huge starry circle appeared above Max’s head, while the roots of the Witch God Tree beneath him pulsed with cursed light.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Mirror Curse of the Seven Dead Shadows."
The seven shadows moved at once.
One attacked his body.
One attacked his bloodline.
One attacked his soul.
One attacked his senses.
One attacked his movement.
One attacked his energy flow.
And the last one attacked the cursed eye on his shoulder, trying to use the Witch’s curse mark as a bridge to drag the entire curse deeper into Max’s existence.
Caroline’s expression changed completely. "Max, careful! She is trying to use the Witch’s mark against you."
For the first time, Nancy’s hand tightened around her sword with real anxiety.

A witch using an existing curse as a medium was far more dangerous than creating a curse from nothing. The little eye attached to Max had already proven impossible to remove or destroy with brute force. If Morgana managed to connect to it, then even Max’s dragon scales might not be able to protect him fully.
Morgana’s eyes flashed with cold delight.
The seven shadows reached Max.
The one targeting the cursed eye arrived first.
But just as its shadowy hand touched the little eye, something unexpected happened.
The little eye blinked.
A faint red-black ripple spread from it.
The shadow froze for an instant.
Max looked down slightly, and his expression remained calm.
"You chose the wrong bridge."

chapters.title: Chapter 1786: Her Three Moves!
paragraphs: Black flames suddenly erupted from his shoulder, wrapping around the cursed eye without burning it. At the same time, seven-colored lightning flickered once around his body, and the golden-black dragon scales released a deep draconic pressure.

The shadow trying to touch the curse mark began twisting violently, as if the Witch’s curse itself refused Morgana’s control. Before Morgana could react, Max lifted his left hand and crushed the frozen shadow with raw physical pressure.
Then Dragonheart moved again.
This time, Max slashed seven times.
Each slash was short, accurate, and merciless.
The first shadow was severed at the neck.
The second was split from shoulder to waist.
The third was pierced through the forehead.
The fourth had its violet eyes cut apart.
The fifth was cut through the knees.
The sixth was divided at the core where its curse threads gathered.
The seventh, the one that had tried to touch the Witch’s mark, was cut last. Max’s blade passed through it silently, and the shadow broke apart into red-black sparks and violet dust.
The Mirror Curse of the Seven Dead Shadows collapsed.
The blackened ground returned to normal.
The starry circle above Max shattered.
Morgana’s face finally changed.
This time, she could not hide it.

Max had not merely defended against the curse. He had broken every part of it and even used the strange resistance of the Witch’s own mark to ruin her attempt to control it. The very curse she had wanted to exploit had refused to become her tool.
Max looked at her calmly.
"Third move."
The words were simple, but they struck Morgana’s pride like a slap.
The witch from Stellar Templar clenched her fingers.
Her purple eyes became icy, and the playful cruelty on her face disappeared completely. The first move had been cut. The second had failed. She had one move left, and everyone was watching.

Rosaline, Kaiden, Orion, Selene’s remaining faction members, Caroline’s group, and even the second faction elves who hated Max were all waiting to see whether Morgana Starveil, one of Stellar Templar’s strongest geniuses, could do anything to him after being given three prepared moves.
Morgana took a slow breath.
Then she bit her finger.
A drop of purple-red blood appeared.

The moment that blood fell into the air, the sky above the Witch God Tree darkened. Stars appeared in the daytime gloom, one after another, forming a vast constellation shaped like a closed eye. The air became cold.

The giant roots beneath the battlefield trembled. The cursed remnants of Witch God Valley stirred in the distance, and countless invisible threads gathered around Max, connecting to his footprints, his breath, his sword aura, the lightning traces left from his battle with Selene, and the tiny fragments of power that had spread from his dragon scales.
Morgana’s voice became low and dangerous.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Star-Coffin Curse of the Nameless Witch."
A coffin made of starlight and curse runes formed around Max.
It did not close from the outside.
It formed directly around him, using the traces he had left in the battlefield as anchors. Violet chains wrapped around the coffin, and ancient witch symbols appeared across its surface.

The moment it manifested, Max felt a force trying to bury his body, seal his energy, silence his soul, and erase his name from the battlefield. It was not a simple damaging technique. It was a burial curse, one meant to trap the target between star fate and witchcraft until their existence weakened enough to be killed.
Morgana’s face was pale after using it, but her eyes were filled with cold confidence.
"This is my third move," she said. "Let me see you walk out of this unscathed."
The Star-Coffin Curse closed.
Boom!
Violet starlight surged like a tide.
The coffin swallowed Max completely.

For several breaths, no one could see him. Only the giant coffin stood in the middle of the battlefield, covered in countless curse runes. The pressure it released made even the second faction elves retreat. Caroline’s face became pale, Jessica looked terrified, and Nancy’s eyes were filled with concern.

Even Rosaline, Kaiden, and Orion looked serious because this was clearly no ordinary witchcraft. Morgana had used blood as a price, the battlefield traces as anchors, and the lingering cursed aura of the Witch God Tree as support.
This was exactly why witches were feared.
When they attacked first with preparation, they were the deadliest.
The coffin trembled once.
Then again.
Morgana smiled faintly despite her pale face.
But the smile lasted only a moment.
A crack appeared on the coffin.
Then another.

A thin sword light leaked out from within, not bright, not violent, but quiet enough to make everyone’s heart turn cold. The crack widened. The violet chains broke one after another. The curse runes on the coffin started vanishing, not because they were being destroyed by brute force, but because the connection holding them together was being severed from within.
Morgana’s pupils shrank.
The coffin split open.
Max walked out.
He was completely unscathed.

His golden-black dragon scales remained flawless. His aura had not weakened. His eyes were calm, and Dragonheart rested in his hand with faint traces of Emotion Severing Path lingering along its edge. The Star-Coffin Curse collapsed behind him, breaking into starlight and dust that scattered into the air like the remains of a failed funeral.
The entire battlefield went silent.
Rosaline stared at Max with clear shock.
Kaiden’s expression finally changed slightly.
Orion’s grin slowly returned, but now it carried genuine amazement.
Seraphine and Fin looked as if they had seen a nightmare.
Caroline exhaled shakily, relief flooding her face.
Jessica stared at Max with wide eyes.
Nancy whispered, "He came out... without even a scratch."
Everyone understood what that meant.
Morgana had not been ambushed. She had not been rushed. She had not been forced to defend. Max had given her three moves, and she had used three of her strongest prepared witchcraft techniques.

For a witch of Stellar Templar, that should have been the most dangerous situation for any opponent. When a witch attacked first with preparation, even stronger enemies could die without touching her.
Yet Max had defended against all three.
He had walked out unscathed.
Max stopped several steps away from Morgana and looked at her calmly.
"Three moves are over."
Morgana’s face turned pale.
The violet charms around her trembled faintly, and for the first time, true fear flickered in her eyes.
Max raised Dragonheart.
His voice remained calm.
"Now it is my turn."
Morgana’s face turned pale the moment Max raised Dragonheart.

The confidence she had displayed earlier, the mocking arrogance she had used when she sneered about the rules of the battle royale, and the cruel amusement that had filled her eyes when she bound Max with the roots of the Witch God Tree were all gone now. She had used three of her strongest witchcraft moves with preparation, and each one had failed.

Worse than that, Max had not merely survived them. He had walked out without a single injury, as if her curses, fate needles, shadow mirrors, and star coffin had been nothing more than interesting tricks placed before his sword.
Now it was his turn.
